articles.title: Standard Chartered Revises Stablecoin Market Outlook
articles.text:
Standard Chartered pushes $2T stablecoin forecast to 2030 as transaction volumes grow
The bank identified four distinct stablecoin markets, with USDC leading payments and AI transactions as competition intensifies over reserve yields.
Standard Chartered says stablecoin transaction activity continues to grow even as the market’s overall value has stalled, suggesting existing stablecoins are circulating more frequently rather than new supply driving growth.
In a report shared with Cointelegraph, the bank said it now expects stablecoin market capitalization to reach $2 trillion by 2030, two years later than initially projected, after the market plateaued at roughly $309 billion this year.
Geoffrey Kendrick, StanChart’s head of digital assets research, said stablecoin usage continues to expand despite slower supply growth, with existing stablecoins changing hands more frequently as their use cases diversify.
Kendrick identified four distinct markets, each with different competitive dynamics. Tether’s USDt (USDT) dominates emerging-market savings, while Circle’s USDC (USDC) leads developed-market payments. USDC and Ethena’s USDe have established strong positions in crypto trading, while USDC also leads the much smaller market for transactions between AI agents.
The bank expects the most intense competition in developed market payments, where challengers such as USDG, M^0 and multibank stablecoin networks are pursuing alternatives to existing payment infrastructure.
According to Kendrick, how issuers and payment networks divide the yield generated by stablecoin reserves could ultimately determine which competitors gain market share.
Related: Crypto’s billions are back, but the premiums aren’t
US regulatory and accounting changes could shape stablecoin use
Standard Chartered’s revised forecast comes as regulatory and accounting developments in the United States could influence how businesses use stablecoins.
Since the GENIUS Act passed in 2025, US regulators have proposed rules governing stablecoin issuance, reserve requirements and consumer protections. Some measures have also clarified the limits of those protections, including a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) proposal that would exclude stablecoin holders from pass-through deposit insurance.
The Treasury Department has also advanced implementation of the law. In August, it proposed rules restricting stablecoin issuance in the United States to federally or state-authorized issuers, with the licensing requirements expected to take effect in January 2027.
Separately, in August, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB), which sets US accounting standards, proposed an update that could affect how companies report certain stablecoins on their balance sheets.
Blockchain payments company Tempo said the proposed changes could make it easier for businesses to use stablecoins for payments and settlement without introducing additional accounting complications.
Related: Crypto Biz: Wall Street and crypto fight for the same turf

articles.title: Solana Sets a Date for Its Next Major Upgrade - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Alpenglow activates on Solana mainnet in epoch 1064, which starts on Wednesday, October 21, at approximately 15:00 UTC, according to the Solana Foundation.
- The upgrade replaces TowerBFT and targets transaction finality of roughly 150 milliseconds, down from about 12.8 seconds today.
- Vote transactions will leave blocks, so Solana's headline transaction counts and TPS figures will drop sharply without any drop in real activity.
Solana has locked in October 21 for Alpenglow, a full replacement of the system its validators use to reach consensus. The switch is tied to epoch 1064, which the Solana Foundation expects to begin around 15:00 UTC that Wednesday.
Alpenglow retires TowerBFT, the current system the network uses, and aims to make transactions final in roughly 150 milliseconds. Finality is the moment a transaction becomes irreversible, and under TowerBFT that currently takes about 12.8 seconds.
On Solana today, a payment is confirmed pretty quickly, but that’s not a guarantee. Until TowerBFT runs out its 13 second clock, the block could in theory still be dropped.
That small doubt is why anyone handling real money tends to wait out the full window. With finality at around 150ms, the irreversible answer arrives almost as fast as the optimistic one, which is what a checkout counter taking SOL or a DeFI application, or a trading desk settling a position actually needs.
TowerBFT works by having validators post their votes as on-chain transactions, and a block only counts as final once 32 slots’ worth of those votes pile up. Votor, the voting protocol shipping with Alpenglow, takes votes off the chain, so validators message each other directly, package the votes into certificates, and can lock in a block after a single round of voting, or two at most.
When 80% or more of stake backs a block in the first round, it finalizes on the spot. If support lands between 60% and 80%, a second round with 60% thresholds decides whether the block is finalized or skipped, and the Foundation says the design tolerates 20% malicious stake plus another 20% offline.
It’s time.
Alpenglow goes live on mainnet-beta Wednesday, October 21, ~14:50 UTC.
18 months of work for a migration that happens in one slot. Finality drops from seconds to ~150ms.
Make sure to follow us @anza_xyz as we countdown to go-live.
Details: https://t.co/MEf26uzCMW
— Anza (@anza_xyz) October 13, 2026
Ordinary users don’t need to do anything, and wallets and apps should behave as they do now. The Solana Virtual Machine, transaction formats, programs, and fees are left alone, while for developers the “confirmed” and “finalized” commitment levels become one and the same.
Each vote account also needs 0.8 SOL on top of its rent-exempt balance to pay the new Validator Admission Ticket, a per-epoch fee of the same size that gets burned. It replaces the roughly 1 SOL per epoch validators spent on vote transaction fees under TowerBFT, and a validator that can’t cover it sits out voting and block production for the following epoch.
The feature gate turns on as epoch 1064 begins, yet TowerBFT stays in charge for another 5,000 slots, roughly 18 minutes, before Alpenglow takes control at slot 459,653,000. This assures stability and prevents any issues during transition.
Validators approved Alpenglow in September 2025, when the SIMD-0326 proposal passed with 98.27% of votes cast in favor. In May, Anza Lead Economist Max Resnick told Decrypt the team was looking at a late Q3 or early Q4 mainnet activation, so everything is going according to schedule.
October 21 delivers only Votor, the first half of Alpenglow. Rotor, a replacement for Turbine, the system Solana uses to broadcast block data between validators, comes later and still has no date.

articles.title: Bitcoin Gives up $82,000 as Hot US CPI Sends Bonds Toward New Highs
articles.text:
Bitcoin price dips below $82K as high oil prices spike US CPI inflation
Bitcoin fell below $82,000 while bond yields targeted new 24-year highs on the back of hot US CPI inflation.
Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $82,000 after Wednesday’s Wall Street open as US consumer inflation beat expectations.
Key points:
- Bitcoin dropped to $81,926 on Bitstamp after US September CPI inflation came in at 3.7% versus expectations of 3.6%.
- Fuel-price increases accounted for the lion’s share of the gain at 9.1% year-on-year.
- US bond yields spiked on the news, while gold fell to $4,079 per ounce.
Bitcoin slips under $82,000 on higher US CPI print
Data from TradingView showed crypto, gold and stock-market futures dropping after the release of Consumer Price Index (CPI) for September.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
At 3.7% year-on-year, this came in 0.1% above majority market consensus, data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) confirmed. The increase in fuel prices around the Middle East conflict and oil-supply crisis was conspicuous.
“The index for gasoline rose 9.1 percent in September, accounting for over half of the monthly all items increase. The energy index increased 5.2 percent over the month following a 2.1-percent increase in August,” an official release stated.
US CPI 12-month % change. Source: BLS
Inflation nonetheless increased across the board, as core CPI — the index minus energy and food — also came in 0.1% higher than anticipated at 2.6% year-on-year.
Commenting, Sonu Varghese, chief macro strategist at Carson Group, suggested that elevated figures should be a foregone conclusion.
“The only surprise is that investors keep getting surprised by broad-based inflation. And we’ve yet to see the full impact of higher diesel prices and the AI boom,” he told CNBC.
The latest data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool showed markets adjusting expectations of Federal Reserve policy as a result of the data. The majority now favored a 25-basis-point interest-rate hike at the Fed’s upcoming meeting on Oct. 28, with the odds of that outcome at 53.7% versus 22.1% the day prior. For December, meanwhile, the odds of a second 25-basis-point hike stood at 50%.
Fed target-rate probabilities for October FOMC meeting (screenshot). Source: CME Group
“Taken in combination with the soft payroll numbers in the September employment report, the FOMC is probably on hold for any rate moves at the upcoming October 27-28 meeting although with a definite bias toward a hike in December,” said Theresa Sheehan, economic analyst at Econoday.
As Cointelegraph reported, the next key US inflation data release, the September print of the Producer Price Index (PPI), is due on Friday.
Analysis: High CPI “last thing global bond markets needed”
Gold fell as low as $4,079 per ounce on the back of the CPI result, while US bond yields spiked.
Related: CryptoQuant’s 3 charts keeping Bitcoin’s ‘Uptober’ thesis valid
The 10-year yield, highly sensitive to energy-price triggers, hit 5.329%, around three basis points off new 24-year highs.
“This is the last thing global bond markets needed. Prior to this number, it looked like the global bond sell-off was calming, but now bond markets are catching on fire again,” economist Robin Brooks wrote in a blog post.
US 10-year bond yield one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
BTC price action continued to circle a key area between $82,500 and $83,400, with analysis still waiting for the market to make a decision on its status as support.

articles.title: ‘Bunker Mode’ Won’t Protect Your Crypto, Critics Say
articles.text:
‘Bunker mode’ won’t protect your crypto, critics say
Even if Justin Drake’s prediction that AI could break cryptography proves correct, critics say “bunker mode” is an impractical suggestion that’s unlikely to protect your crypto.
If rising geopolitical tensions weren’t enough cause for concern, now it’s crypto’s turn to go nuclear.
The industry is busy debating a cryptography doomsday scenario in which attackers derive private keys from public keys using a formerly far-fetched, but now potentially credible, AI scenario that places everyone’s crypto at risk.
Ethereum researcher Justin Drake called for “bunker mode” planning last Wednesday, citing “humbling” advances in artificial intelligence that could accelerate the discovery of mathematical attacks and ultimately “break” cryptography:
“IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA [Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm] breaks before Qday, in the worst case in months not years.”
Drake thinks the industry should begin planning a controlled migration of assets to fresh addresses whose public keys have not been exposed, reducing the information a potential attacker could exploit.
But what is he basing this warning on, and is there genuine cause for alarm?
Is the crypto panic justified?
Drake’s concern is not just whether AI will speed up the arrival of quantum computers able to break cryptography, but that AI systems might also help discover mathematical attacks using classical computing that human cryptographers have missed.
He argues that elliptic curves — the cryptography that underpins most blockchains — may be more vulnerable to such breakthroughs than hash functions because of their greater mathematical structure, which raises the possibility of a classical algorithm breaking elliptic curve cryptography.
Justin Drake wants the industry to plan for bunker mode. Source: Justin Drake
Matthew Green, a cryptography professor at Johns Hopkins University, weighed in on Drake’s assessment, adding fuel to the flames of panic already ripping through the crypto industry.
“I think we might lose public key cryptography,” he said.
Related: Too big to pause: Could an AI slowdown crash the economy?
Not everyone shares their alarm. Coinbase’s head of cryptography, Yehuda Lindell, said that, to his knowledge, there is “no evidence whatsoever” that the decades-old mathematical assumptions underpinning elliptic curve cryptography have been weakened.
Lucien Bourdon, Bitcoin analyst at hardware wallet Trezor, tells Magazine:
“There are no credible published advances against the math behind ECDSA, with AI or anything else.”
He says that none of OpenAI’s recent releases of AI-written math papers contain an attack on ECDSA — although Drake believes that’s cause for suspicion rather than comfort. Drake’s other argument is that elliptic curves have more mathematical structure than hash functions, which could make them easier to break.
“He doesn’t say how,” Bourdon says. “He also calls his timeline a worst-case scenario and tells people not to rush.”
Zach Herbert, chief executive and cofounder of hardware wallet FoundationHQ, tells Magazine that moving funds to fresh addresses may not be enough if an extended public key (xpub) has already been shared with a wallet app or third party.
In that case, “they already have the information needed to derive the public keys you’re trying to hide,” he says.
And as Taylor Monahan, founder and chief executive of Ethereum wallet MetaMask, pointed out, if cryptography breaks, the price of your bags won’t be your only concern:
“If elliptic curves are broken so that any exposed public key leads to compromise and it’s by a financially-motivated hacker whose top priority is to steal crypto, the entire fu**ing world is going to zero. Having your magic internet coins in bunker mode is not going to help you.”
Why moving coins may not be enough
Herbert says xpubs let wallets generate multiple public keys for the same account, including those for addresses that have never been used.
If a wallet app or third party already has that information, moving funds to a fresh address within the same account may not hide the new address’s public key from them.
If ECDSA became practically breakable, “an attacker could recover the corresponding private keys without ever touching your hardware wallet.”
Related: Dragonfly partner rejects ‘bunker mode’ doomerism, calls for proactive blockchain measures
“No, it’s obviously not sufficient protection,” Eli Ben-Sasson, co-founder and chief executive of Ethereum scaling protocol StarkWare, tells Magazine.
“Other than just moving your coins, if you want to use them ever again, you would need to download new kinds of wallets.” 
He says a break would affect more than wallet signatures, too. Ethereum’s infrastructure-level signatures and consensus mechanisms would also need attention, as would the Kate-Zaverucha-Goldberg (KZG) polynomial commitment scheme used for data in blobs.
“Finally, gas prices would likely also increase dramatically, because a lot of the functionality would break,” he adds.
On Bitcoin, some address types conceal the full public key behind a cryptographic hash until the coins are spent. If the relevant hash functions remain secure, this could provide an additional layer of protection against an attacker trying to derive a private key from a public key. Taproot addresses, by contrast, expose a public key directly onchain.
Creating a P2PKH public key hash to receive payment. Source: Bitcoin.org
Bourdon says common SegWit addresses, which begin with bc1q, keep public keys hidden until spending, and wallets like Trezor generate fresh receiving addresses to limit address reuse.
“There’s nothing to do right now,” he says, adding that a panicked migration will do more harm than good. “People who rush to move funds make mistakes, and scammers use stories like this one to reach them.”
It’s also worth noting that any time you spend a Bitcoin, the public key gets exposed in the mempool anyway, providing a window of opportunity for an attack.
Not all crypto assets are created equal
Some blockchains are already preparing for cryptographic threats, although their proposed solutions vary.
On AI-focused NEAR Protocol, users can add a quantum-safe FIPS-204 key to an existing mainnet account in a single transaction, without moving their assets, and wallets like Meteor support quantum-safe signing. This relies on lattice based cryptography, which Ethereum creator Vitalik Buterin worries may also be vulnerable to attack.
Ethereum is developing a broader post-quantum roadmap using hash based signatures and ZK proof aggregation, that covers everything from transaction signatures to consensus and data security. It also has an emergency hard fork and recovery proposal mapped out on paper.
In a March 2024 post, Vitalik Buterin outlined a potential hard fork that would roll back blocks following the onset of mass theft, disable conventional wallet transactions and let users reclaim funds by using zero knowledge proofs of a seed phrase.
Related: Vitalik Buterin backs crypto ‘bunker mode’ amid rapid AI math advances
Max Shannon, senior research associate at Bitwise Europe, says that remains a proposal with “no set timeline.”
While no one has shown a working attack as of yet, he says users should switch to quantum-safe signatures “over the long term.”
Hardfork in a quantum emergency. Source: Eth Research
Starknet’s account abstraction architecture allows users to switch signature schemes without migrating funds to a new address. Ben-Sasson says the core technology doesn’t need to be changed, “because account abstraction means you can take any signature scheme.”
But he says other components still need attention, including parts of the network’s state tree and its reliance on Ethereum for security.
Switching to a new address isn’t going to help users on Solana, as public keys are exposed by default — though they can migrate funds to a post quantum vault like Winter Wallet.
Solana Foundation technology vice president Jacob Creech said Solana users would not need to enter “bunker mode” if its signature scheme became breakable.
A network upgrade could let users prove ownership of their secret seed using a hash-based proof and migrate their accounts to a safer signature scheme. A working proof of concept exists, he says, though the upgrade itself has not been deployed.
So, should crypto holders be panicking?
Shannon says Bitwise isn’t worrying about this theoretical risk for now, but it’s “worth being prudent over.”
“We can discuss fresh addresses and xpub exposure as a thought experiment,” Herbert says, “but I wouldn’t pretend those steps amount to a practical plan for that scenario.”
Because some people have old devices, complicated multisignature arrangements, or Bitcoin they haven’t touched in years, he says a software update “would not automatically protect those coins.”
Bourdon reminds crypto holders to scrutinize the source, since Drake’s warning was accompanied with talk of Ethereum’s moves toward the hash-based cryptography he recommends.
“So the warning about an unproven threat doubles as a pitch for Ethereum’s roadmap,” he says.
While that doesn’t prove Drake wrong, there is still no evidence that ECDSA is about to be broken, and plenty of risks involved with rushing to move funds.
But if the cryptography underpinning crypto wallets and blockchains does fail, moving coins may be the easiest part of the industry’s response.
Magazine: Crypto lending rises again… but have they solved the risks?

articles.title: Standard Chartered Opens Bitcoin and Ethereum Trading to Wealthy UAE Clients - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Standard Chartered launched direct Bitcoin and Ethereum trading for affluent UAE clients on Wednesday after receiving licensing approval from Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority.
- Eligible Professional Investor clients can buy and sell BTC and ETH through their existing bank accounts, with the bank handling custody and settlement in a closed-loop model built with SC Ventures-backed Zodia Markets.
- The bank called the service a global first for Standard Chartered and plans to expand it to other markets, though it gave no timeline.
Standard Chartered will now let its wealthier clients in the United Arab Emirates buy and sell Bitcoin and Ethereum straight from their bank accounts, the British lender announced Wednesday.
The move eliminates the need for its affluent clients to rely on separate wallets or third-party platforms, the bank said.
The service opens first to clients classified as Professional Investors and runs under licensing approval from Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, or VARA. The bank called it a global first for Standard Chartered and the first crypto trading offering from an international bank in the UAE.
Trades are executed inside the bank's own ecosystem, and Standard Chartered handles custody and settlement end-to-end through what it calls a closed-loop model, which the bank says reduces clients' exposure to third-party wallet risk.
The bank built the product across its Wealth and Retail Banking and Corporate and Investment Banking units, working with Zodia Markets, a digital asset trading firm backed by Standard Chartered's venture arm, SC Ventures.
“As client interest in digital assets continues to grow, this launch represents a significant milestone for Standard Chartered as we bring digital assets into our core wealth offering” Samir Subberwal, the bank's global head of wealth solutions, retail products, data and analytics, said. He argued that clients now want more than access, and are looking for the security that comes with buying through a regulated institution.
Rola Abu Manneh, Standard Chartered's CEO for the UAE, Middle East and Pakistan, said the country was a natural choice given its regulatory environment and its role as one of the bank's four global wealth hubs.
Until now, Standard Chartered's crypto trading business had catered to institutions. In July 2025, it became the first global systemically important bank—one of the lenders regulators consider too big to fail—to offer spot trading in Bitcoin and Ethereum to institutional clients, through its U.K. branch.
It brought that institutional desk to the UAE last month through its unit in the Dubai International Financial Centre, which is overseen by a different watchdog, the Dubai Financial Services Authority. The bank's crypto custody service had already gone live in the UAE in September 2024, and in the European Union through a Luxembourg entity a few months later.
Wealth clients previously had indirect routes into crypto at the bank: crypto exchange-traded funds on its cash equities platform, structured products, and over-the-counter derivatives tied to crypto prices. The new service lets them own the coins themselves, held by the bank, rather than a product that tracks their price.
The bank has historically been very bullish towards crypto, with frequent calls from its analysts for Bitcoin to extend to new highs.
In June, Geoff Kendrick, Standard Chartered's global head of digital asset research, declared crypto winter over after Bitcoin slid to nearly $59,000, a 53% drop from its October 2025 peak of $126,000. The bank has held onto a $100,000 year-end target for BTC.

articles.title: Canada Crypto Remittances to Asia Surge 141% to $2.36
articles.text:
Canada crypto remittances to Asian countries surge 141% to $2.36B: Chainalysis
Remittance-sized crypto transfers from Canada to three Asian countries reached $2.36 billion, while transfers to the Philippines alone rose 28% to $61 million.
Remittance-sized crypto transfers from Canada to India, China and the Philippines surged 141% year-over-year to $2.36 billion, as digital asset payments expanded across the three major remittance corridors.
According to a new Chainalysis report, the three countries accounted for 19.4% of Canada’s outbound cross-border stablecoin value, up from 10.9% in the previous year. Transfers totaled 3.56 million transactions in the 12 months ending June 2026, averaging $663 per transaction.
Referring to additional data shared with Cointelegraph, Chainalysis head of research Eric Jardine said Canada-to-Philippines crypto remittances alone reached $61.02 million across 73,564 transactions, up 28% and 34.7%. The analysis covers Bitcoin and stablecoins above $10,000 to and from personal wallets.
Chainalysis ranked Canada as the strongest peer-to-peer (P2P) crypto economy among G7 nations, pointing to its large foreign-born population and the cost of traditional remittance services as potential adoption drivers.
Stablecoins gain ground in Canada’s remittance corridors
About 23% of Canada’s population is foreign-born, the highest share in the G7, according to Morva Rohani, executive director of the Canadian Web3 Council.
“Remittance corridors to India, the Philippines, Nigeria, Pakistan, and China are heavily used,” Rohani said in the report.
Stablecoins accounted for 44% of Canadian dollar-based order book volume in June, up from 30% a year earlier, the report found. Chainalysis cited World Bank estimates putting the average cost of sending money from Canada at 6.7%, although low blockchain settlement fees do not account for currency conversion and cash-out costs.
Related: China P2P stablecoin wallets grew 43x despite crypto restrictions: Chainalysis
The report also found that Canada’s domestic P2P activity tracked changes in its temporary visa-holder population since mid-2021, although Chainalysis cautioned that the relationship was correlational rather than causal. Jardine told Cointelegraph that the firm does not limit its analysis to the smallest transfers to avoid “omitting real remittance value.”
Previous Chainalysis research found global cross-border stablecoin flows rose 77.5% to $220.3 billion in the year through June.

articles.title: 'It Can Take Years': Coinbase Presses for Bitcoin Quantum Migration to Start Now - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Coinbase, which says it custodies roughly 5% of all Bitcoin, urged developers to start preparing for the quantum threat now, warning that consensus changes and migration “can take years.”
- It laid out technical requirements—backing a flexible “container” design like BIP-360, a staged “1-of-2” classical-plus-quantum spending path, and compatibility with the MPC key-splitting custodians rely on.
- The exchange said dormant, lost, and Satoshi-era coins are a separate governance problem.
Coinbase is pressing Bitcoin’s developers to begin preparing for the quantum-computing threat before it’s too late, laying out a detailed technical wish list for how the network should harden itself and arguing the work can’t wait for certainty that a threat has arrived.
In a blog post published Tuesday, the exchange, which says it custodies roughly 5% of all Bitcoin in existence, framed the shift to quantum-resistant cryptography as a complex, multi-year undertaking that needs to start now.
“Bitcoin consensus changes and ecosystem migrations can take years,” the company wrote, warning that waiting for the announcement of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer, the kind capable of breaking Bitcoin’s signatures, would leave too little time to respond.
The concern centers on how Bitcoin secures wallets. A sufficiently powerful quantum machine could, in theory, derive a private key from an exposed public key and drain the funds, a hypothetical milestone the industry calls “Q-Day.”
Coinbase stressed that a fix involves far more than picking a new signature scheme: any transition would need to protect both existing and newly created coins, fit Bitcoin’s limited block space, keep working for ordinary wallets and institutional custody alike, and offer a migration path for coins that never move.
The post reads less like a mandate than a set of requirements from one of the network’s largest stakeholders. Coinbase backed a flexible “container” design, pointing to proposals such as BIP-360, that would let new post-quantum signature systems be swapped in over time without a full redesign.
It also floated a staged “1-of-2” construction, letting the same funds be spent with either a classical key or a quantum-safe one during the transition. The company emphasized that whatever scheme Bitcoin adopts should be compatible with multi-party computation, the key-splitting technique custodians like Coinbase rely on to guard against theft.
Thornier still is the question of dormant, lost, or exposed coins, including Satoshi-era holdings, which Coinbase said should be treated as a separate governance problem. It cautioned that any rescue mechanism must itself be quantum-safe, so an attacker who only knows an exposed public key couldn’t exploit it.
The push builds on Coinbase’s steady drumbeat of quantum warnings.
The exchange convened a quantum advisory board in January o study the risks and develop precisely the sort of guidance it offered this week. The company also joined a Bitcoin Security Consortium in July alongside BlackRock and Strategy, pledging a combined $15 million toward quantum-proofing Bitcoin.

articles.title: Qivalis Receives EMI Authorization from Dutch Central Bank for Euro Stablecoin
articles.text:
Qivalis wins Dutch e-money license for euro stablecoin
Qivalis said the Electronic Money Institution authorization enables it to launch a euro-denominated stablecoin, with issuance planned for the coming months, subject to additional MiCA requirements.
European banking consortium Qivalis received Electronic Money Institution (EMI) authorization from the Dutch central bank, bringing it closer to issuing a euro-denominated stablecoin.
The Amsterdam-based company revealed the license from De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) in a Wednesday announcement shared with Cointelegraph.
Qivalis said the EMI license subjects it to ongoing supervision by the central bank and makes it eligible to issue euro-denominated electronic money tokens.
The approval clears a key regulatory hurdle, bringing Qivalis closer to issuing its euro-denominated stablecoin under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). The company plans to begin issuance within the coming months, subject to applicable MiCA requirements and the publication of its white paper.
Qivalis is looking to introduce a euro-denominated stablecoin into a market largely dominated by US dollar-based stablecoins. Tether USDt’s (USDT) $183 billion market capitalization accounts for over 60% of the total $303 billion stablecoin market, according to DefiLlama.
“We believe Europe should have a euro-denominated on-chain settlement asset issued under European law and subject to European regulatory standards,” said Jan-Oliver Sell, CEO of Qivalis.
In May, Qivalis added 25 new banks across 15 countries, expanding to a total of 37 institutions backing it.
Related: Standard Chartered expands Bitcoin and Ether trading to professional investors in UAE

articles.title: Bitcoin Falls as Hot Inflation Puts a Fed Hike Back on the Table - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- U.S. consumer prices rose 3.7% year over year in September, above the 3.6% forecast, as gasoline jumped 9.1% in a single month.
- Odds of an October Fed rate hike roughly doubled from 22% after the report, and the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 5.3%.
- Bitcoin fell 1.5% to $82,142 and is holding the $81,847 to $82,305 Fibonacci golden zone, with $81,603 as the next support.
Bitcoin fell 1.5% to $82,142 on Wednesday after U.S. inflation came in hotter than expected, dragging most of the crypto market down with it. Ethereum dropped 2.8% to $2,440, Solana lost 1.9% and XRP slid 1.3%, while total crypto market cap shed 0.7% to $2.8 trillion.
The Consumer Price Index rose 0.6% in September and 3.7% over the past year, up from 3.4% in August, per the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Economists expected 3.6%. Gasoline prices jumped 9.1% in a single month and accounted for more than half of the increase.
Core CPI, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 2.6% annually against a 2.5% forecast. That is the reading the Federal Reserve watches most closely, since it shows whether price pressure is spreading into rent, airfares, and services.
Expensive gasoline starts with expensive oil, which has traded above $90 a barrel for most of the past two months amid the war between the U.S. and Iran. Pricier fuel raises the cost of shipping and producing almost everything.
When inflation runs hot, the Fed raises interest rates to cool spending. It already hiked in September to a 3.75%-4.00% range, and traders now see roughly 44% to 49% odds of another hike at its October 27-28 meeting, up from 22% before the report, according to CME FedWatch.
The 2-year Treasury yield, which closely tracks Fed rate expectations, jumped about 10 basis points to roughly 4.9%, while the 10-year climbed to about 5.3%, near 24-year highs.
Higher yields hit crypto directly. A government bond paying 5.3% with almost no risk competes with Bitcoin, which pays nothing. Rising rates also make borrowing more expensive and tend to strengthen the dollar, draining the cheap money speculative assets feed on, which is why the S&P 500 fell 0.6% and the Nasdaq 0.8% on the same news.
Crypto also swings harder than stocks because many traders borrow to bet on rising prices, and when the price drops past a set level, exchanges automatically close those positions, a process called liquidation, and that forced selling can push prices lower and trigger more liquidations in a chain.
At the moment, more than $281 million in crypto derivatives positions have been liquidated in the past 24 hours, with most of it coming in just the last four hours—and the majority of that coming from Bitcoin long positions (the bulls betting the price would go up, and now paying the price when it dropped).
Bitcoin price: The macro picture is punching hard
On the daily chart, Bitcoin opened at $83,066 and now trades near $82,211, sitting inside the Fibonacci "golden zone" it reclaimed on Tuesday. That zone marks an area where pullbacks within uptrends often attract buyers.
The average price of the last 50 days remains above the 200-day average, a setup traders read as an intact long-term uptrend. The Average Directional Index, which gauges trend strength on a 0-to-100 scale where readings above 25 confirm a trend, sits at 27.7 with buyers still ahead, down from 29.9 on Tuesday, meaning traders are bullish, just not as much as they used to be.
The Relative Strength Index, a momentum gauge from 0 to 100, slipped to 48.7, just under the 50 line that separates bullish from bearish momentum. The Squeeze Momentum Indicator has been on for eight sessions, meaning volatility is compressed and a big move is building, and its -0.76 reading leans bearish by a small margin.
A daily close below $81,603 would break the golden zone and bring the $80,365 swing low into play, with the trend band near $80,284 right under it; losing that would expose $78,003. On the upside, bulls need to reclaim $84,245 before targeting $85,301, $86,644 and the October high of $87,422.
The next test arrives Thursday with the Producer Price Index, which tracks what businesses pay for goods and services, and the Fed announces its rate decision on October 28.

articles.title: Kraken’s Parent to Buy Lithuanian Saldo Bank amid TradFi Expansion
articles.text:
Kraken parent to buy Lithuanian Saldo Bank amid TradFi expansion
Payward expects to close the acquisition in 2027, enabling it to expand its traditional banking services into four EU operating markets already served by Saldo Bank.
Cryptocurrency exchange Kraken’s parent company, Payward, will buy Lithuania-based Saldo Bank as part of its expansion into traditional financial services, calling it “a deliberate next step in an infrastructure strategy we’ve been building for years.”
Payward signed a definitive agreement to acquire Saldo Finance Oy, a Finnish holding company whose subsidiary, Saldo Bank UAB, is a digital bank licensed in Lithuania, according to a Wednesday announcement.
Payward said Saldo Bank’s EU banking license and footprint will enable it to expand into four operating markets, including Lithuania, Finland, Sweden and Germany, where the bank already offers retail term deposits. The bank’s authorization is also passported into the Netherlands.
The acquisition is expected to close in 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals. It would enable Payward Banking to offer traditional banking services, including interest on deposits, lending products and banking-as-a-service, such as card issuance, passporting and lending capabilities to small and medium enterprises.
“A regulated EU bank is the piece that lets us serve European clients the way a primary financial institution should: one place to hold assets, move them freely, and put them to work,” said Payward co-CEO Arjun Sethi.
In August, Payward launched a multi-asset debit card in the US through Kraken’s payment app, Krak, allowing customers to spend crypto and fiat while earning up to 2% cashback in dollars or Bitcoin.

articles.title: Hex Founder Richard Heart Detained in Istanbul on Interpol Red Notice: Report - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Turkish police and intelligence officers detained Hex founder Richard Heart in Istanbul on Wednesday, Turkish media reported, acting on an Interpol Red Notice.
- Finland sought the notice in 2024 on a charge of aggravated tax fraud, and Heart was detained along with his wife, according to the reports.
- The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission accused Heart in 2023 of raising more than $1 billion in unregistered crypto offerings, but later dropped the case.
Turkish authorities have detained Richard Heart, the founder of the Hex cryptocurrency, in Istanbul on an Interpol Red Notice, Daily Sabah reported on Wednesday, citing Turkish news agency IHA.
Heart, whose legal name is Richard James Schueler, was detained with his wife on Wednesday morning in an operation by Istanbul police and Turkey's National Intelligence Organization (MIT), according to the report. Police had monitored his address in the city's Beşiktaş district before the arrest.
Officers seized a dozen mobile phones, several laptops, graphics cards, rifles, pistols, two drones, gold bracelets and a large amount of cash in different currencies, IHA reported.
A Red Notice is a request to law enforcement worldwide to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition or similar legal action, and is not an international arrest warrant. Interpol issued the notice for Heart in 2024 at the request of Finland. The notice lists a single charge, aggravated tax fraud, though Finnish authorities have also sought him over an alleged assault. Daily Sabah described the notice as relating to high-value cryptocurrency fraud.
Heart and Hex
Heart launched Hex in 2018, marketing it as a high-yield "blockchain certificate of deposit."
In 2023, the SEC charged Heart and three entities he controlled, Hex, PulseChain and PulseX, with conducting unregistered offerings of crypto asset securities that raised more than $1 billion. It also accused him of misappropriating at least $12 million of investor funds to buy luxury goods, including sports cars, watches and a 555-carat black diamond known as "The Enigma."
A federal judge dismissed the complaint in February 2025 for lack of jurisdiction, finding that Heart's activities were not clearly aimed at U.S. investors. The SEC declined to amend it by an April deadline, ending the case, which Heart's lawyer called "a complete victory."
It was not immediately clear whether Finnish authorities have requested Heart's extradition from Turkey.

articles.title: Hardware Wallet Buyers Face Tampering They Cannot Easily Detect
articles.text:
Can crypto users trust the supply chain behind hardware wallets?
Ledger hardware wallet implants have renewed scrutiny of the middlemen handling devices before they reach buyers, even through authorized sellers.
Ordinary cryptocurrency owners cannot realistically be expected to detect sophisticated tampering with hardware wallets, security researcher Joe Grand told Cointelegraph on Tuesday.
Grand specializes in hardware security and has helped recover cryptocurrency from locked wallets. His work includes developing techniques to bypass security protections and extract data from memory chips used in wallets made by Trezor and KeepKey.
“It’s really hard to explain to people how they’re supposed to look at their devices, because even technical people like me are not looking at every single device to see if it’s been tampered with,” Grand said.
The concerns surfaced Friday after crypto losses were reported involving Ledger devices sold through CryptoBilis, a reseller listed as authorized in Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines. Ledger confirmed Saturday that one affected device contained an unauthorized implant.
Malicious implants in Ledger wallets sold by CryptoBilis captured users’ recovery phrases and transmitted them over cellular networks, the French hardware wallet maker said.
More control doesn’t mean less trust
Hardware wallets are designed to keep private keys offline, reducing exposure to online attacks that can target software wallets.
Some hardware wallets have achieved global popularity, and their distribution networks have created opportunities for supply-chain tampering.
Crypto analyst Mati Greenspan told Cointelegraph that he has never used a hardware wallet despite being involved in the industry since 2013, seeing little value in adding another chain of trust.
Related: MediaMarktSaturn pulls Ledger products amid tampering reports
“When you buy a hardware wallet, you’re introducing a whole new chain of trust, from the manufacturer to the supplier to whoever handled the device before it reached you,” Greenspan said.
Nick Neuman, CEO of Bitcoin security company Casa, said avoiding third-party trust entirely is impossible. “There is always an intermediary you will need to trust,” he said, adding that users should spread their risk across multiple providers rather than rely on just one.
Security checks cannot catch everything
Trezor, among Ledger’s main rivals, said its devices undergo authenticity checks and accept only signed firmware, but acknowledged that these protections cannot rule out physical tampering.
“You can also check that the packaging and holographic seal are intact and look for unusual marks on the device, but these checks alone cannot guarantee that it has not been modified,” a Trezor spokesperson told Cointelegraph.
Related: Ledger asks resellers to halt sales in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong
The company said the implants found in Ledger devices pose a different challenge because they capture information from the screen without modifying the firmware. Trezor said that it has not observed this type of attack on its own devices.
On Tuesday, Trezor announced that it would reduce the number of resellers as a “preventive” step.
Hardware wallet designs can reduce tampering risks
Grand suggested several physical design changes, from transparent casings that expose internal components to tamper-resistant enclosures that would force attackers to recreate the housing to conceal modifications.
“It’s going to be a lot harder for an adversary to inject additional hardware into the device, because they would have to recreate the entire housing,” he said.
The security researcher also pointed to anti-tamper design recommendations from electronics engineer Dave Jones, while cautioning that such measures should not be relied on alone. They could make supply-chain attacks more difficult, but would not eliminate the risk.

articles.title: Ledger Asks Resellers in Seven Asian Markets to Pull Devices After Suspected $86M Drain - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Ledger has asked resellers and distributors in six Southeast Asian countries and Hong Kong to suspend sales of its devices while it investigates tampered wallets.
- The company said the only confirmed incidents remain in Southeast Asia, and that it has not verified a drain linked to a device bought elsewhere.
- MediaMarkt Saturn has stopped selling Ledger devices in its stores and online after a customer in Germany reported an implant, though no funds were lost.
Ledger has asked resellers and distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to stop selling its hardware wallets and take them off the shelves while it investigates devices fitted with a hidden implant, the company said in a tweet on Tuesday.
The request covers Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong.
Incident Update - Oct 13th, 2026
Ledger is asking resellers and distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to suspend sales of Ledger devices while the investigation is ongoing. This includes taking products off the shelves.
Specifically the countries are: Indonesia,…
— Ledger (@Ledger) October 13, 2026
The only confirmed incidents remain in Southeast Asia, Ledger said, and it has not verified a drain linked to a device bought elsewhere. The company has previously said that all confirmed losses involve devices sold through CryptoBilis, a reseller in the region.
Ledger is still working to establish who tampered with the devices and at what point in the distribution chain. It said it has no indication that its own infrastructure, systems, services or direct sales channel have been compromised.
Ledger's Donjon security team found that the implant reads the 24-word recovery phrase from the device's screen during setup and sends it out over LTE. Anyone holding that phrase can restore the wallet and move its funds. Onchain investigator Specter has traced more than $86 million in suspected thefts, a figure Ledger says it has not verified.
Earlier on Tuesday, MediaMarkt Saturn stopped selling Ledger devices in its stores and online, with Ledger's agreement, after a customer in Germany reported an implant, Ledger said in a separate tweet. No loss of funds was reported.
Rival hardware wallet maker Trezor said on Tuesday that it will end its authorizations for resellers on January 1, 2027, describing the move as a "precautionary measure." Trezor said there was no evidence that its own devices had been compromised.

articles.title: Coins.ph Says BSP License Intact Amid Reported Revocation Risk
articles.text:
Coins.ph says Philippine central bank license intact amid revocation claims
Coins.ph says its Philippine central bank license remains intact amid reports of possible revocation over alleged offshore gambling transactions.
[Update, 11:00 am UTC: Added a follow-up response from a Coins.ph spokesperson.]
Coins.ph said it remains licensed by the country’s central bank following reports that it could face license revocation over alleged transactions involving restricted offshore gambling operators. 
Coins.ph is one of the largest crypto exchanges in the Philippines, recording approximately $52 million in 24-hour spot trading volume on Wednesday, according to CoinGecko. The reported license risk follows restrictions imposed by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) on incoming InstaPay and PESONet transfers involving DCPay Philippines, the entity operating Coins.ph’s peso e-wallet services.
“Coins.ph firmly denies any claim that it knowingly serves offshore gaming or gambling operators,” the company said in an official statement shared with Cointelegraph on Wednesday. “Our users’ funds are safe; we continue to operate as a BSP-licensed institution,” it added.
Asked whether transactions involving offshore gambling operators had been processed through its platform, the Coins.ph spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the exchange does not accept or permit such operators and continuously screens customers and transactions in line with BSP requirements. The company did not directly confirm or deny whether such transactions had occured.
BSP restrictions target Coins.ph payment services
In an earlier advisory, Coins.ph said the BSP had instructed it to strengthen internal controls. The company said cash-in services and QRPh collections were temporarily unavailable, while crypto trading, cash-outs, bill payments and merchant QRPh payments remained accessible. QRPh payments are the central bank’s national QR standard.
Local media outlet BitPinas reported that the restrictions were imposed under BSP Monetary Board Resolution No. 839. DCPay holds an electronic money issuer license, while Betur Inc. operates the exchange’s crypto asset services under a separate virtual asset service provider license. The restrictions reportedly targeted DCPay’s payment operations rather than Betur’s crypto services.
Related: Philippines eyes payment operator registration freeze, tighter VASP checks
In 2025, the central bank ordered supervised financial institutions to remove links providing access to gambling websites from their payment applications. However, the BSP has not publicly linked that directive to the restrictions on Coins.ph.
Cointelegraph also sought confirmation and comment from the BSP. A central bank representative said they would look into the inquiry but had not provided further comment at the time of publication.

articles.title: Notorious Crypto Celeb Meme Coin Promoter Plots Second Wave on New Launchpad - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Floyd Mayweather's social media accounts promoted a Solana-based meme coin on Monday, which peaked at a $1 million market cap before plummeting in value.
- Notorious celebrity coin promoter Sahil Arora is claiming responsibility for the token and says it's the start of another wave coming to the blockchain.
- Arora has faced accusations of "scamming" celebrities and "rug pulling" tokens, since he exploded onto the scene in 2024 by creating a Caitlyn Jenner meme coin.
Sahil Arora, the notorious promoter behind a string of 2024 celebrity meme coins, just launched a new one, with Floyd Mayweather’s social media accounts briefly promoting it. Arora told Decrypt it’s the start of a comeback: he wants to revive the celebrity coin craze on Solana trading platform Fomo, the same trick that made his name on Pump.fun.
Arora made his name through a series of celebrity-linked meme coin launches on Pump.fun in 2024. It started with former Olympian Caitlyn Jenner, who went on to claim that Arora "scammed" her. Since then, he has been tied to several other projects that celebrities and industry experts have labelled as "rug pulls" or simply fraudulent.
His latest entry is the Floyd Money Mayweather meme coin launched on Fomo, which peaked at just a $1 million market cap before plummeting 96% over the next three hours on Wednesday.
Mayweather's social media account promoted the token, according to several social media accounts, before selling from the deployer wallet for just $5,000 worth of profit and deleting the posts. The token then pumped to its $1 million market cap peak, which meant the wallet lost out on major profits—but Arora says this was all part of the plan.
The coin promoter told Decrypt that the entire scheme was orchestrated, explaining that the narrative of Mayweather fumbling gains was what pushed the token's price higher. Fomo is a trading platform that blends social media elements, meaning that you can see who is buying and selling—which can create viral moments.
Arora claims to have profited seven-figures on the Mayweather token by selling from other wallets. However, on-chain analytics firm Bubblemaps doesn't think that is realistic. The biggest connected cluster of wallets profited approximately $105,000, Bubblemaps told Decrypt, and the top 100 traders combined only made $306,000 worth of profit. So, the analytics firm said numbers aren't adding up.
Still, it appears that the crypto coin promoter stood to profit handsomely from the scheme and is plotting to do it again.
JUST IN: FLOYD MAYWEATHER CREATES A FOMO ACCOUNT AND SHILLS A MEMECOIN
HE SOLD FOR $5,000 PROFIT BEFORE THE COIN RAN, MISSING OUT ON OVER $280,000 IN PROFIT pic.twitter.com/UAX2KWpo5x
— Market Insider (@MrketInsider) October 13, 2026
"We will recreate everything on Fomo that we made on Pump.fun in 2024, just with better strategies where people also win," Arora told Decrypt. When pushed on the new strategies, he said, "this wasn’t [sold in] one clip," in contrast to previous projects that have faced "rug pull" accusations after dropping more than 90% in seconds.
He added that he is "tight" with all of the celebrities that he launches tokens with, and convincing them to be part of his schemes is "really easy."
In 2024, Pump.fun provided Arora with a platform to easily create tokens for celebrities to promote via social media chatter. Now, Fomo has created a trading environment that drives virality, and Arora wants to take advantage of that.
This isn’t Mayweather’s first crypto rodeo. In 2017, he asked fans to start calling him Floyd 'Crypto' Mayweather, dropping his usual 'money' moniker, as he started to plug a streak of token sales.
One of those sales was the Centra Tech initial coin offering, or ICO, which raised $32 million for a crypto debit card it told investors was backed by Visa and Mastercard—it wasn't. By 2018, he was charged by the SEC for promoting the sale without disclosing that he'd been paid. He later agreed to pay a fine and not promote any security for three years.
But in 2021, he gained even more heat for his promotion of an obscure Ethereum-based token named EthereumMax. The boxer turned up to a Bitcoin conference wearing an EthereumMax and was booed by the crowd for suggesting other tokens could succeed in front of a crowd of Bitcoin maximalists. Mayweather was named alongside Kim Kardashian in a lawsuit regarding EthereumMax, though the judge dismissed it by the end of 2022.
This Arora-linked token is just the latest chapter in Mayweather’s long, messy history with crypto.
Floyd Mayweather did not respond to Decrypt's request for comment.

articles.title: Solana sets October 21 for massive Alpenglow upgrade that could make transactions 99% faster to finalize
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Solana has scheduled its Alpenglow upgrade for Oct. 21, targeting a 99% reduction in transaction finality times.
- The upgrade could cut finality from 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds, accelerating settlement for payments, trading and tokenized assets.
- The network must replace its existing consensus system while operating, with validator coordination critical to a successful migration.
Solana will replace its blockchain's consensus system on Oct. 21, targeting transaction finality in approximately 150 milliseconds.
On Oct. 13, Anza, the blockchain network's core developer, announced the mainnet activation date, setting the stage for one of the most significant infrastructure changes in Solana's history.
The upgrade, known as Alpenglow, will replace TowerBFT, the mechanism that currently takes approximately 12.8 seconds to finalize transactions. If successful, the change would reduce finality times by nearly 99%, bringing the network closer to instantaneous settlement.
The planned overhaul follows Solana's recent reduction in block-production times to about 200 milliseconds, another improvement designed to speed up transaction processing.
However, Alpenglow addresses a different limitation: the delay between processing a transaction and the point at which the network considers it irreversible.
Solana targets faster settlement for payments and financial markets
Under Solana's existing consensus mechanism, validators establish finality by submitting votes as blockchain transactions, with agreement accumulating across multiple blocks.
Alpenglow introduces a new system called Votor, which allows validators to exchange votes directly and combine them into cryptographic certificates. This lets blocks become final after one or two voting rounds, significantly reducing the time needed to reach network-wide agreement.
According to the Solana Foundation, the change could benefit financial applications that depend on finalized transactions before releasing funds or executing subsequent operations.
For instance, payment providers could reduce the time between receiving a transfer and treating the funds as settled, while trading platforms could complete settlement-dependent operations more quickly.
The improvement could also strengthen Solana's position in tokenized assets and stablecoin payments, where reliable settlement is essential for transferring value between financial institutions and applications.
Importantly, the 150-millisecond figure remains a performance target rather than an established mainnet result. Actual finality will depend on network conditions, validator participation, and the number of voting rounds required.
The upgrade also leaves transaction execution unchanged, so existing applications will largely continue operating without modifying their underlying programs.
Meanwhile, removing validator votes from blockchain transactions should free up capacity for user activity, though it could also cause an apparent decline in Solana's reported transaction counts.
A separate component of Alpenglow, known as Rotor, which will overhaul how blocks are distributed across the network, is planned for a later release.
Live-network migration puts validator readiness to the test
Despite the potential performance gains, implementing Alpenglow requires Solana to replace its consensus system while the blockchain remains operational.
According to the migration schedule, activation will begin around 15:00 UTC on Oct. 21, at the start of epoch 1064.
However, the network will continue running TowerBFT for another 5,000 slots (about 18 minutes) before attempting the transition to Votor.
The handover requires validators representing at least 82% of staked SOL to sign a genesis certificate, establishing a common starting point for the new consensus system.
During the transition, user transactions will briefly stop being included in blocks, with normal processing expected to resume once the new system takes over.
Validator operators must also prepare their infrastructure beforehand.
The upgrade requires software built on Agave 4.3.0, while Firedancer and Frankendancer clients will not be supported during the migration. Validators must additionally maintain at least 0.8 SOL above their rent-exempt balance to cover a new participation fee.
Those who fail to meet the funding requirement will be excluded from voting and block production in the next epoch.
Alpenglow has already completed deployments on Solana's testnet and devnet, providing opportunities to identify problems before the mainnet transition.
However, those rehearsals do not guarantee the same results in production.
The October 21 migration will therefore provide the first live-network evidence of whether Solana can safely replace its consensus system and consistently deliver finality near the 150-millisecond target.c

articles.title: Bitcoin Demand Analysis Keeps BTC Price ‘Uptober’ Hopes Alive
articles.text:
CryptoQuant’s 3 charts keeping Bitcoin’s ‘Uptober’ thesis valid
Bitcoin onchain analysis eyed a “potential bottom” for BTC price action in early October as demand weathered external headwinds.
Bitcoin (BTC) can still preserve its traditionally strong October performance, as onchain data points to a local BTC price bottom forming.
Key points:
- Onchain data suggested that Bitcoin could still end October strong, following historical patterns.
- Bitcoin exchange reserves remained 1.7% lower than in mid-September, while whales avoided selling.
- Apparent demand neared a transition to positive readings for the second time in 2026.
BTC price analysis flags “potential bottom” signals
New analysis published on crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant Monday show onchain conditions in a state of “cautious optimism.”
Bitcoin continues to weather mixed macroeconomic and geopolitical headwinds, which include 24-year highs in US bond yields, rising oil prices and cooling capital inflows to exchange-traded products. These conditions have dampened optimism over Bitcoin delivering a strong performance in October.
“Now, signs of a potential bottom are emerging,” CryptoQuant contributor XWIN Research Japan wrote.
Since the start of October, conditions have changed to increasingly benefit crypto and risk assets. XWIN points to cooling expectations of interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve into 2027, boosting the odds of inflows improving. At the same time, markets expect more clarity over the US domestic political situation after the approaching Midterm Elections.
“Less political uncertainty after the vote could help investors reassess allocations,” XWIN continued.
Bitcoin exchange reserves, apparent demand and whale holdings give XWIN reasons to believe that October’s local low may have already occurred.
The BTC supply on exchanges has fallen from 2.726 million on Sept. 20 to 2.68 million as of Tuesday, a decrease of 1.7%, despite a modest increase over the past week.
Bitcoin exchange BTC reserves. Source: CryptoQuant
At the same time, the combined holdings owned by large-volume investors, or whales, remain above 3 million BTC. The cohort’s urge to reduce exposure has survived BTC/USD dropping from $87,000 on Oct. 2 to near $80,000 on Oct. 8.
Bitcoin whale holdings (screenshot). Source: CryptoQuant
Bitcoin demand data stays bullish in October
Apparent demand, a measure that compares newly mined BTC with changes in dormant supply, shows overall demand remains supportive.
Related: Bitcoin keeps up pressure on $84K as US stocks skirt Korea tech sell-off
The metric has been negative throughout 2026, with a brief period of positive 30-day readings in the second half of August. Since then, demand has been negative, but has recovered to near-neutral levels as of this week.
“These developments suggest conditions for a bottom are improving. Confirmation requires sustained ETF inflows, stronger US spot buying and continued demand recovery,” XWIN said.
“‘Uptober’ need not mean uninterrupted gains: a correction can build the foundation for the next advance.”
Bitcoin apparent demand growth. Source: CryptoQuant
This week, crypto asset manager Bitwise said that Q3 onchain data pointed to “crypto spring” after historically significant performance. CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju, meanwhile, announced what he saw as the start of a new crypto bull market in late August, calling the bear market “over.”

articles.title: Morning Minute: Move Over, Saylor, There’s a New Top Buyer in Town - Decrypt
articles.text:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors rebound ahead of CPI; BTC at $83.6k
- Vivek’s Strive bought $280M in BTC last week, 13x Saylor’s buys
- BTC and ETH ETFs flip back to inflows, ETH breaks 10-day outflow streak
- STRC hits $99.90 and highest level since May depeg
- Solana core dev announces Alpenglow live on October 21 on mainnet
🟠 Move Over, Saylor, There’s a New Top Buyer in Town
For five years, “who bought the most Bitcoin this week” had one answer. That’s quietly stopped being true.
Vivek’s Strive Asset Management (Nasdaq: ASST), run by Matthew Cole, just scooped up 3,311 BTC for roughly $280 million between Oct. 5 and 9, buying the dip at an average of ~$84,500 as the market sold off. It’s Strive’s biggest single purchase since January, and it caps a genuine tear: $94.5M in late September, $169M in early October, then $280M. Total stack now sits at 32,773 BTC, about $2.73 billion.
In that same stretch, Michael Saylor’s Strategy bought 250 BTC for about $21.5 million. Strive outbought Strategy by roughly 13 to 1.
This isn’t a one-week fluke of timing. Strategy’s buying has shrunk for two straight weeks, and that same week it spent nearly nine times more buying back its own preferred shares ($192M) than it spent on Bitcoin. Its mNAV just dropped below 1.0 for the first time, meaning the market values the company at less than the Bitcoin sitting on its balance sheet.
Now to level set by total holdings, this isn’t remotely close. Strategy still sits on 848,250 BTC—a ~$51 billion position, more than 25 times Strive’s stack. Saylor isn’t being dethroned as the king of Bitcoin treasuries. But “biggest holder” and “most aggressive buyer right now” have, for the first time, become two different titles.
The newcomer is accumulating at the pace the pioneer has abandoned—and it just told us how it plans to keep going. Strive is selling 5 million shares of a new preferred at $100 a piece, a $500 million raise paying a fixed 15% daily, with proceeds earmarked for more Bitcoin. That’s a 15% annual coupon—$75 million a year in cash out the door—which is a very expensive way to be right. But with STRC at $99.90, Saylor’s BTC faucet is about to turn back on, too. Let the battle of the Bitcoin giants begin…

articles.title: Coins.ph users face app lockout as central bank intervenes
articles.text:
Quick Take
- The platform says customer funds are safe and that it is working to restore services after reports about its operations.
- The company says its controls exclude offshore gambling operators and that it continues to operate as a BSP-licensed institution.
- Its Oct. 14 statement gives no restoration date, while a separate advisory leaves regulator-set compliance timelines undisclosed.
Philippine crypto platform Coins.ph said users’ funds were safe and that it was working to restore affected services in an Oct. 14 statement.
The response follows news reports about offshore gaming transactions and the company’s engagement with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), the Philippine central bank.
A separate, undated company advisory on internal controls said the BSP directed Coins.ph to introduce enhancements to those controls. Coins.ph said it is working with the central bank to meet requirements within the regulator-set timelines.
Coins.ph’s assurances come as it acknowledges that it still needs to restore affected services. For customers, the message addresses the status of their funds and its operational plans in the same response. The return of those services remains expected, with details to follow.
In the statement accompanying the X post, Coins.ph said it maintains strict controls to keep offshore gaming and gambling operators off its platform. It noted that it is committed to serving only legitimate, compliant businesses.
On licensing, the company described itself as a regulated and licensed platform, adding on the statement:
“Our users’ funds are safe; we continue to operate as a BSP-licensed institution.”
The company asserts that it remains licensed while assuring customers their money is safe.
Coins.ph also said it continues to strengthen compliance and control functions and works closely with regulators to enhance its operations. Separately, the advisory said it is working to meet the BSP’s requirements, without giving a completion date.
The Oct. 14 statement expects full restoration “soon,” but does not identify the affected services, say when the disruption began, or provide a calendar date for their return. For users awaiting those services, it leaves the restoration timetable unspecified.
Coins.ph said it will share further updates through official channels and asks users to follow them. The separate advisory promises updates as services are restored. Those updates are where the company says it will report progress, following its current reassurance about funds and its stated expectation of a return to full service.

articles.title: What’s the Case for Supreme Court Review of Sam Bankman-Fried’s Conviction?
articles.text:
Sam Bankman-Fried’s lawyer lays out ex-FTX CEO’s Supreme Court case
Should US high court justices grant review of the case, they could release a decision as early as June 2027.
After being convicted in 2023, losing his appeal to a Second Circuit court in 2026 and awaiting a decision on a presidential pardon that may never come, former FTX CEO Sam “SBF” Bankman-Fried is hoping to take his criminal case to the US Supreme Court.
Jeffrey Fisher, counsel at the law firm Hecker Fink LLP and representing Bankman-Fried in his Supreme Court of the United States (SCOTUS) appeal, spoke to Cointelegraph about the potential timeline surrounding the former FTX executive’s case and what onlookers could expect to see should the justices choose to accept his petition for a writ of certiorari, possibly resulting in a new trial.
Bankman-Fried is pursuing the high court’s review while also seeking a pardon from President Donald Trump. According to Fisher, SCOTUS rules require SBF to file a petition for a writ of certiorari within 90 days of a decision from an appellate court, requesting that the justices consider the case.
The Supreme Court initially gave the US government until Oct. 15 to respond to SBF’s petition, but it already granted an extension to Nov. 16, which could allow the justices to decide whether to hear the case in late 2026 or early 2027. If the court grants review of his client’s case, it could issue a decision in the current term, which ends in June 2027, or during its next term, which begins a year from now.
Bankman-Fried was convicted on seven felony fraud counts related to the misuse of customer funds by FTX, the cryptocurrency exchange he founded and led, and which filed for bankruptcy in November 2022. He was sentenced to 25 years in prison and ordered to pay $11 billion in forfeiture.
‘Assets are fine’: Why FTX’s losses and recoveries were irrelevant at trial
Bankman-Fried’s petition to the Supreme Court presents two main arguments for justices, should they consider the case, based on lower courts weighing “evidence indicating victims lost money” and that the $11 billion forfeiture order following his conviction violated the Eighth Amendment’s prohibition on “excessive fines.”
“The Supreme Court has expressed concern over the years for prosecutorial overreach in criminal fraud prosecutions,” Fisher told Cointelegraph. “This kind of evidence introduced in this prosecution raises a real question about prejudice to the defendant.”
Related: US Senate unanimously adopts resolution opposing clemency for SBF
The argument presented by prosecutors at SBF’s criminal trial and reiterated by the Second Circuit ruling found it was “immaterial as a matter of law” whether the former CEO had the funds and planned to repay FTX’s victims for their losses at the crypto exchange.
“As the district court made clear, FTX customers were defrauded as soon as Bankman-Fried transferred their money to Alameda regardless of how strongly he believed he might later return the money,” the Second Circuit said in its June 2026 decision.
According to Fisher, this theory differs from many fraud cases in which a defendant “swindled people out of money and enriched himself at their expense.”
“Our whole point is the theory the government chose makes it irrelevant whether any customers lost money or, if so, how much,” the lawyer said.
The Supreme Court petition noted that the highest court had ruled in Kousisis v. United States in 2025 that prosecutors could “seek decades-long prison sentences anytime people are induced by misrepresentations to part with their money — even if they suffer no pecuniary harm.”
SBF’s lawyers instead argued the 2007 ruling by the First Circuit in United States v. Carpenter, in which a defendant “intended all along to ensure his customers suffered no financial losses,” was more applicable to the FTX case. The appellate court initially ruled in that case that a jury’s decision may have been based on “moral disapproval“ rather than evidence related to fraud.
Mark Bini, a former federal and state prosecutor and currently a partner at Reed Smith, told Cointelegraph he believed that the chance that the court would accept SBF’s arguments and grant a new trial “seems low,“ but the conditions around forfeiture were “really interesting“ based on the size: $11 billion. He called reliance on United States v. Carpenter instead of Kousisis v. United States an “uphill battle“ for Bankman-Fried, legally.
While many FTX users were eventually paid out for their losses at the exchange beginning in 2025, the token values were based on the price at the time of the 2022 collapse, meaning many could have missed gains in the three years between bankruptcy and repayments.
How forfeiture could affect SBF’s ‘future livelihood’
Bankman-Fried’s forfeiture order could follow him long after his release from prison, potentially allowing the government to make claims on his future earnings. The former FTX CEO is expected to remain in prison until 2043.
“He has no money to pay it,” said Fisher. “Under the terms of the penalty, it is an $11 billion debt for the rest of his life, to the government. Any dime he would ever make upon release would have to be turned over to the government [...] There’s rules, maybe he gets to keep a dime.”
If the court accepts the forfeiture argument but rejects the claim that SBF had a right to present evidence related to repaying users, Bini said it’s more likely to reduce the forfeiture amount than to warrant a new trial.
“It’s a huge forfeiture amount and there is this tension because the case law is such that the government is entitled to seek both forfeiture and restitution,” said the Reed Smith lawyer, adding: “It’s a very unusual case where the defense is arguing that ‘gosh, everyone is being made whole’ [...] yet you have this tremendous forfeiture.”
Cointelegraph reached out to the Justice Department for comment on the case but did not receive a response.
Caroline Ellison now employed at a charitable organization
Former Alameda Research CEO Caroline Ellison, one of the central figures tied to the downfall of FTX, has been working at Manifund, a charitable fundraising organization connected to the effective altruism movement, after serving time in prison as part of a plea agreement with US authorities.
According to Manifund co-founder and CEO Austin Chen, Ellison began on a work trial at the company on July 13, about six months after she was released from federal custody. She accepted a full-time role on Aug. 10.
“I believe in redemption,” said Chen. “Caroline has admitted her faults, worked to make creditors whole, and served her time in prison. I’d like to give her the opportunity to contribute back to the world; I hope that the world will concur.”
In a rare public statement, Ellison said that she was “grateful to Austin for giving me a second chance, and judging me on my current work performance rather than my past.”
Many of the comments on Chen’s Substack post were extremely negative, ranging from calling Ellison’s hiring an “extremely rogue move” to an action showing “truly terrible judgment.”
“[Ellison is] a cynical opportunist who stole billions, and got a sweetheart deal because prosecutors were willing to give everything up to get Sam,” said Coin Metrics co-founder Nic Carter. “She was extremely lucky that she got such a light sentence. The utmost shame on you for attempting to rehabilitate her.”

articles.title: Kraken Owner Payward to Buy Lithuania's Saldo Bank in EU Push - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Payward, the parent company of crypto exchange Kraken, is buying Saldo Bank, an EU-licensed lender based in Lithuania, the Financial Times reported.
- Co-CEO Arjun Sethi said customers will be able to borrow and lend against their assets without selling them, in an undisclosed deal expected to close in 2027.
- The deal comes as a U.S. community bank lobby sues the federal bank regulator over the trust charters it has granted to crypto firms.
Payward, the parent company of crypto exchange Kraken, is buying Lithuania-based Saldo Bank as it expands into lending and card issuing, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.
Payward is the first digital asset company to buy a bank in Europe, according to the FT. Saldo received its EU banking license in 2021 and offers consumer and business loans as well as term deposits. The price was not disclosed.
"One of the biggest things that our customers have been asking us is 'I would like to get products and services and offerings similar to what I get with another bank,'" Payward co-CEO Arjun Sethi told the FT.
Sethi said the plan is to bring cash, crypto, tokenized stocks and credit together in a single system, so customers can borrow and lend against their assets without selling them.
Crypto charters in the U.S.
The Wyoming-based company, founded in 2011, applied in May for a national trust company charter from the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the federal bank regulator. Coinbase and Ripple are among the crypto firms that have received conditional approval for such charters, which let them hold customers' assets and provide transaction services but not take deposits.
This month, the Independent Community Bankers of America sued the OCC, arguing that granting such charters to crypto firms exceeds the regulator's authority. "Any non-fiduciary firm seeking the benefits of a federal bank charter should meet the same standards as community banks," ICBA President and CEO Rebecca Romero Rainey said in a statement. An OCC spokesperson declined to comment.
The bank deal follows Payward's $550 million acquisition of derivatives exchange Bitnomial in April and its $600 million purchase of Asian stablecoin payments firm Reap Technologies in May. Kraken filed confidentially for an IPO last November, but has since pushed the listing back to the second quarter of 2027 at the earliest, CoinDesk reported in September, citing people familiar with the matter.
The Saldo acquisition is subject to regulatory approvals and is expected to close in 2027.
