articles.title: Bitcoin Standard Author says Bitcoin Will Become ‘Less Volatile’ and Larger Than Gold
articles.text:
Bitcoin will become ‘less volatile’ and larger than gold: ‘The Bitcoin Standard’ author
Saifedean Ammous argues that Bitcoin already functions as money when held as a store of value; expects it will become larger and less volatile than gold as it matures.
Saifedean Ammous, the author of the 2018 academic book “The Bitcoin Standard,” said that Bitcoin already functions as a medium of exchange and that volatility’s effect on that is likely to diminish.
Bitcoin (BTC) can serve as a medium of exchange as it becomes less volatile than gold while surpassing the market capitalization of the largest precious metal, wrote Ammous in a Tuesday X post.
“Holding Bitcoin is using Bitcoin as money, and its lack of widespread use as a method of payment is no evidence against its monetization unfolding,” added Ammous.
The remarks come in response to a passage in Professor Lawrence H. White’s book, “Better Money: Gold, Fiat, or Bitcoin?,” which argued that Bitcoin’s fixed supply makes it too volatile to serve as a medium of exchange.
“With no supply response to demand swings, BTC’s price is too volatile for people who want a reliable medium of exchange,” wrote White in a Monday X post, referencing chapter six of his book. He added that the lack of supply response was the reason stablecoins have “eaten BTC’s lunch transaction volume.”
Other industry watchers have also predicted that Bitcoin would eventually surpass gold. In May 2025, Bitwise’s head of European research, André Dragosch, told Cointelegraph that their in-house prediction forecasts a $1 million Bitcoin price by 2029, which would make Bitcoin match gold’s market capitalization.
However, Bitcoin’s current $1.6 trillion market capitalization would need to grow by at least 18-fold to surpass Gold’s near $29 trillion market cap to become the leading global asset.
In April 2025, Blockstream CEO Adam Back predicted Bitcoin will start rivaling gold’s use cases as a monetary hedge, due to global financial instability and rising fiat inflation.
Related: Ledger implant tests Bitcoin ETFs as safer custodial solutions than hardware wallets

articles.title: Surging dollar forces Bitcoin sell-off as rate hike odds double
articles.text:
Quick Take
- September US inflation reached 3.7%, while annual core CPI rose to 2.6%, exceeding the forecasts reported by Reuters.
- October Fed hike odds near 47% after CPI, compared with roughly 20% before the release.
- Higher Treasury yields could pressure Bitcoin ahead of the Oct. 27-28 Fed meeting, even if policymakers hold rates.
Bitcoin faces a tougher interest-rate outlook after US inflation data released Oct. 14 pushed bets on another Federal Reserve hike sharply higher. Rising Treasury yields could weigh on Bitcoin by making interest-bearing dollar assets more attractive.
Market-data provider LSEG data shows money markets priced in roughly a 47% chance of another October rate increase after the release, up from closer to 20% beforehand.
September consumer prices were 3.7% higher than a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics release. Annual core inflation, which excludes food and energy, increased to 2.6% from 2.4%. Both readings exceeded forecasts of 3.6% and 2.5%, respectively.
On a seasonally adjusted monthly basis, headline CPI rose 0.6% after 0.4% in August. Gasoline prices rose 9.1% and accounted for more than half the monthly headline increase, while shelter costs increased 0.4%. Monthly core CPI rose 0.3%, matching August but exceeding the 0.2% forecasts.
After the results, Bitcoin hit an intraday low of $81,588.88 on Oct. 14.
Another increase would extend September's tightening
The Fed had already raised its target range by a quarter percentage point to 3.75%-4.00% on Sept. 16. Another hike would extend that tightening, with the next policy meeting scheduled for Oct. 27-28.
Post-CPI reports put the two-year Treasury yield at 4.872%, up seven basis points on the day, with the dollar showing gains against a basket of currencies. The shift in those markets shows the inflation surprise is changing expectations for borrowing costs ahead of policymakers' next decision.
For Bitcoin holders, the consequence depends partly on whether those higher yields persist. Continued competition from interest-bearing dollar assets could create a headwind for a cryptocurrency that does not pay interest, even if the Fed leaves rates unchanged in October.
The release also followed a period of cheaper short-term volatility pricing. Oct. 12 showed concentrated put options on Deribit at $76,000-$80,000 for the Oct. 16 expiry, which buyers can use to protect against falling prices.
The immediate change is greater market concern about further tightening. It remains unclear whether Bitcoin can withstand that pressure if yields stay elevated as the October Fed decision approaches.
Bitcoin is -1.90% over the past 24 hours and currently sits at rank #1 by market cap.

articles.title: BitMEX Sued in UK for Return of $27M in Bitcoin Over Unlicensed Derivatives - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- UK software engineer Lewis Barber is suing the operator of BitMEX, the crypto derivatives exchange that shut down in September, in London's Commercial Court.
- Barber wants 324.8 BTC returned, alleging BitMEX traded with him without authorization from the Financial Conduct Authority, the UK's financial regulator.
- His lawyers say other UK traders may have similar claims, which could run to hundreds of millions of pounds in total.
A British software engineer is suing the operator of crypto derivatives exchange BitMEX for the return of 324.8 BTC, alleging it traded with him in the UK without regulatory approval, according to The Guardian and particulars of claim reviewed by Decrypt.
The Bitcoin was worth £20.4 million on October 1, the claim says, or about $27.2 million by Decrypt's calculation using the claim's exchange rates.
Lewis Barber, who brought the claim against BitMEX operator HDR Global Trading, entered into around 2,294 trades on the exchange between 2018 and 2022 from five accounts, the claim says. It challenges the 1,053 that lost him money.
All of them were perpetual swaps, a derivative similar to a futures contract but with no expiry date. Each trade was a regulated activity that BitMEX was not authorized to carry out in the UK, the claim argues, so none can be enforced against Barber under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.
The claim says BitMEX did not restrict access from the UK, let new users select it as their country of residence, and ran promotional campaigns worldwide, including an advertisement in The Times in January 2019. It also cites a March 2020 warning from the FCA that BitMEX may have been trading regulated investments in the UK without authorization.
Barber also claims damages for deceit, alleging BitMEX knew it was not authorized when it implicitly represented that it could lawfully trade with him. His solicitors wrote to BitMEX rescinding the trades in December 2025, the claim says.
The claim has been filed but not yet formally served on BitMEX, the Guardian reported. "No such claim has been served on HDR Global Trading Limited," a BitMEX spokesperson told the newspaper.
BitMEX also faces a proposed class action in New York alleging theft of Bitcoin and insider trading, which names co-founders Ben Delo, Arthur Hayes and Samuel Reed.
The three co-founders pleaded guilty in 2022 to violating the Bank Secrecy Act through anti-money laundering failures at the exchange, and were pardoned by President Donald Trump in March 2025. BitMEX itself pleaded guilty to Bank Secrecy Act violations in 2024 and was ordered to pay $100 million in January 2025.
BitMEX in the UK
BitMEX shut down on September 23, having announced in July that it would close.
Delo gave Reform UK £36 million in September, the largest single donation in British political history, Decrypt reported.
Many other investors are likely to be in a similar position to Barber, his law firm Seladore Legal said in a statement shared with Decrypt, putting the potential total at hundreds of millions of pounds.
"Other UK-based persons may have entered into similar contracts with BitMEX, although whether any individual has a claim will depend on the particular facts and trading history," said Gareth Keillor, a partner at the firm.

articles.title: Kraken moves to acquire $181 million European bank in major push beyond crypto trading
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Kraken parent Payward agreed to acquire Lithuania-based Saldo Bank, which held €163 million in assets at the end of 2025.
- The deal would add €137 million in deposits and a €113.5 million loan book, deepening Payward's expansion beyond crypto trading.
- The purchase price remains undisclosed, while European regulatory approval is required before the targeted 2027 closing.
Kraken's parent company, Payward, has agreed to acquire a European bank as it expands beyond cryptocurrency trading into traditional financial services.
On Oct. 14, the company announced a definitive agreement to purchase Saldo Finance Oy, a Finnish holding company that owns Lithuania-based Saldo Bank.
The acquisition would give Payward control of a licensed European banking institution with approximately €163 million ($181 million) in assets, offering deposits, lending and payment services across multiple markets.
The transaction, whose financial terms were not disclosed, is expected to close in 2027, subject to regulatory approval.
It marks another step in Payward's effort to build a financial services platform that can handle traditional money and digital assets while reducing its dependence on external banking partners.
Kraken targets European banking expansion with Saldo acquisition
Saldo Bank is an established but relatively small European financial institution whose operations have expanded considerably in recent years.
According to its 2025 audited financial statements, the bank held €162.9 million in assets at the end of December, up about 22% from €133.6 million a year earlier.
Its net loan portfolio increased to €113.5 million from €95.4 million, while retail deposits climbed 24% to €136.9 million.
The bank also reported its first annual profit of approximately €962,000 in 2025, reversing a €2.4 million loss the previous year. Its operating profit before impairment losses rose to €10.4 million, though credit impairment charges absorbed most of it.
These figures show that Payward is acquiring an operating lending business with an established deposit base, although its balance sheet remains modest compared with major European financial institutions.
More importantly, Saldo's existing infrastructure provides a foundation for expanding Payward's financial products across Europe without establishing a new banking operation from scratch.
The institution currently operates in Lithuania, Finland, Sweden, and Germany, and is authorized to expand into the Netherlands. It provides retail term deposits across its operating markets, consumer lending in three countries, and business loans in Lithuania and Finland.
Its credit card business is already operating in Finland, with a Swedish expansion planned for 2027. Saldo also provides embedded lending services that allow fintech companies to offer credit products through its infrastructure.
Payward plans to build on these capabilities by introducing interest-bearing deposits, business and consumer lending, card issuance, and SEPA payment services for European customers.
The acquisition could also support a broader banking-as-a-service business, allowing other financial technology companies to access regulated financial infrastructure through Payward.
Payward co-CEO Arjun Sethi said the transaction forms part of the company's strategy to establish deeper financial relationships with customers. Sethi said:
“We believe whoever owns that relationship earns the right to serve everything around it.”
The strategy builds on Payward's efforts to gain greater control over financial infrastructure.
In March, its Wyoming-chartered subsidiary, Kraken Financial, secured a limited-purpose Federal Reserve master account, providing direct access to US payment infrastructure.
The company also holds an electronic money institution license from the Central Bank of Ireland and says its existing banking operations have originated more than $2 billion in loans.
Meanwhile, Payward expanded its payment capabilities in July by acquiring Reap, a stablecoin-focused company offering card issuance and cross-border transaction infrastructure.
The Saldo acquisition would extend these capabilities into regulated European deposit-taking and lending, potentially allowing Payward to offer banking, cryptocurrency trading and payment services through a more integrated platform.
The firm stated:
“We’re not acquiring a bank to be a bank. We’re acquiring the infrastructure to let Payward serve European clients the way a primary financial institution should: one place to hold assets, move them freely, and put them to work.”
European regulatory approval remains key to banking expansion
However, Payward's ability to implement its plans depends on securing regulatory approval and complying with the restrictions attached to Saldo's specialized banking license.
Under Lithuanian banking rules, specialized banks can accept deposits, issue loans, and provide payment services but face restrictions on certain investment activities.
Consequently, ownership of Saldo would not automatically authorize Payward to integrate every cryptocurrency or investment product into the acquired bank.
The transaction will also require supervisory scrutiny of Payward's financial position, management arrangements, and compliance systems.
Beyond regulatory approval, Payward would assume responsibility for maintaining a banking balance sheet, including credit risk, deposit liabilities, and capital requirements.
Saldo's latest financial statements showed total equity of €16.3 million at the end of 2025, with a common equity Tier 1 capital ratio of 14.9% and a total capital adequacy ratio of 19.8%.
These capital measures are key as Payward considers expanding the bank's loan book and other services after the acquisition.

articles.title: Standard Chartered Expands UAE Bitcoin and Ether Trading to Professional Investors
articles.text:
Standard Chartered expands Bitcoin and Ether trading to professional investors in UAE
Standard Chartered expanded its spot crypto trading services to professional investors in the UAE region, with plans to offer access to more market participants.
Standard Chartered has expanded Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH) trading to wealthy clients in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) who qualify as professional investors.
Eligible investors can trade these assets within their existing Standard Chartered bank accounts, the London-headquartered multinational bank announced Wednesday.
Standard Chartered’s eligibility criteria require individuals to have at least 4 million dirhams (about $1.1 million) in net assets, excluding their main residence, and sufficient investment knowledge and experience or representation by a licensed entity.
Digital assets are “moving into mainstream wealth conversations,” and the bank’s clients are increasingly looking for the “security, trust and confidence that comes from investing through a regulated and trusted institution,” said Samir Subberwal, global head of wealth solutions, retail products, data and analytics at Standard Chartered.
The development comes over a month after Standard Chartered launched UAE crypto trading services for institutional clients in early September.
Standard Chartered is not the only company expanding its digital asset offering in the region. On Monday, cryptocurrency exchange Kraken’s parent company, Payward, received VARA approval to provide crypto services through its local entity. In July, neobank Revolut received in-principle approval from Dubai’s VARA to offer crypto-related services.
Related: XRP treasury Evernorth’s shares rise 5% at Nasdaq opening print

articles.title: Ripple targets trillion-dollar securities markets with new US brokerage and South Korean deals
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Ripple secured partnerships with DriveWealth and Meritz Securities to expand its stablecoin, custody and tokenization services into global capital markets.
- The agreements could bring RLUSD into brokerage settlement while expanding Ripple's reach across South Korea's regulated securities industry.
- The partnerships open new commercial opportunities, but neither announcement establishes revenue expectations or a complete deployment timetable.
Ripple announced partnerships with DriveWealth and Meritz Securities to extend its services across global brokerage and securities markets.
The two agreements, announced on Oct. 14, will bring Ripple's stablecoin, payments, and custody infrastructure into DriveWealth's brokerage operations while exploring securities tokenization opportunities with South Korea's Meritz.
DriveWealth, which provides investment infrastructure to more than 100 partners worldwide, plans to integrate Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin into European settlement operations, with potential expansion into the US. Meanwhile, Meritz becomes Ripple's first Korean securities-firm partner and fourth institutional partner in the country this year.
The agreements deepen Ripple's expansion beyond cross-border payments into traditional capital markets, where financial institutions are exploring blockchain technology to reduce settlement delays, manage collateral and tokenize financial assets.
They also come as South Korea prepares to introduce a regulatory framework for tokenized securities in February 2027, potentially opening another market for Ripple's institutional infrastructure.
DriveWealth brings RLUSD into global brokerage infrastructure
Under the DriveWealth agreement, the brokerage infrastructure provider will integrate RLUSD on the XRP Ledger to support settlement in Europe, alongside Ripple's stablecoin issuance and redemption capabilities.
The integration addresses a longstanding challenge in international investing: stock trading has become increasingly accessible outside conventional market hours, while the banking infrastructure used to fund transactions still operates under geographic and time restrictions.
DriveWealth already supports trading in US equities for 24 hours a day, five days a week. However, international clients can face delays when moving funds across borders, particularly when transfers depend on bank operating hours.
The companies intend to let clients fund and manage collateral accounts with stablecoins that can be converted to cash in near real time, potentially reducing the capital held idle while awaiting traditional bank transfers.
“We've already enabled 24/5 trading; now we need the funding to match,” DriveWealth Chief Executive Officer Naureen Hassan said in the announcement.
The partnership extends beyond stablecoin settlement.
DriveWealth will integrate Ripple Payments to support cross-border funding from its international partners and use Ripple's digital-asset custody infrastructure in Europe, with plans to expand into additional markets.
The companies are also exploring equity financing opportunities through Ripple Prime's Delta One business, which covers institutional services involving US equities and equity derivatives.
For Ripple, the arrangement creates an opportunity to distribute its infrastructure through DriveWealth's existing brokerage network, which serves financial institutions, digital wallets and fintech platforms offering access to US markets.
However, the companies did not disclose expected settlement volumes, financial terms or a timetable for completing every integration.
South Korea deal expands Ripple's institutional reach
Ripple's separate agreement with Meritz Securities extends that capital-markets strategy into South Korea, where financial institutions are preparing for the introduction of regulated tokenized securities.
The companies will initially explore Ripple Custody and tokenization infrastructure within Meritz's existing securities operations, expanding their cooperation as the country's digital-asset regulations develop.
Meritz is evaluating opportunities involving fractional investment products, security tokens, trading platforms, spot exchange-traded funds and won-denominated stablecoins. The agreement does not commit either company to launching those products.
The partnership adds a securities firm to Ripple's growing Korean institutional network, following earlier agreements with Kyobo Life Insurance, Kbank and Jeonbuk Bank.
Those relationships cover tokenized government-bond settlement, digital-asset custody wallets and cross-border remittances, respectively, giving Ripple connections across several functions of the country's financial system.
The latest expansion comes ahead of a major regulatory change.
South Korea's Financial Services Commission has scheduled the first phase of its tokenized-securities framework to begin on Feb. 4, 2027, when amendments to the Electronic Registration Act take effect.
The initial phase will cover selected institutional bonds and money market funds, unlisted shares issued through trust structures and certain fractional investment securities. Broader public securities and stablecoin-linked settlement infrastructure are planned for later stages.
The framework could create opportunities for custody and tokenization providers as securities firms develop systems to issue, record, and transfer blockchain-based financial instruments.

articles.title: Starknet Launches Shadow Accounts for DeFi Wallet Privacy
articles.text:
Starknet introduces wallet privacy feature for DeFi activity
Starknet’s Shadow Accounts allow users to obscure connections between their main wallets and DeFi activity, though transactions remain visible onchain.
Ethereum layer-2 network Starknet has launched a wallet privacy feature that lets users interact with decentralized finance (DeFi) apps without publicly linking activities to their main wallets.
StarkWare, the team behind Starknet, said that its new Shadow Accounts feature creates separate, persistent addresses for individual applications. Users can fund the accounts using shielded balances held in the network’s STRK20 privacy pool. This allows them to maintain lending, trading or other DeFi positions under different onchain identities.
The new privacy feature obscures the connection between the shadow account and the wallet funding it. However, balances, transactions and positions of these shadow accounts remain publicly visible onchain, according to Starknet.
Once integrated into a DeFi application, the feature allows users to connect their wallets, switch from public to private mode and deposit assets into a vault. Their Shadow Accounts then maintain their positions until they withdraw funds back into a shielded balance.
StarkWare said the functionality could eventually extend beyond vaults to liquidity provision, lending, borrowing, staking, derivatives trading, prediction markets and NFT marketplaces.
The launch follows StarkWare’s broader blockchain privacy push. In June, the company introduced its STRK20 privacy framework, which allows private transfers and shielded token balances on Starknet.
Later that month, StarkWare demonstrated a Private Know Your Customer system that enabled users to verify personal information without revealing their full identity documents.
Related: StarkWare unveils Starknet quantum roadmap, says industry has no excuse

articles.title: Ethereum's quantum race takes a new turn as zkSync courts banks and Starknet weighs exit
articles.text:
Quick Take
- zkSync unveiled a real-time Ethereum prover as Starknet considers becoming an independent blockchain to accelerate quantum protection.
- The competing strategies highlight how Ethereum's quantum-security roadmap is reshaping priorities across its Layer-2 ecosystem.
- zkSync is courting banks while Starknet weighs independence, but neither strategy has established a sustainable commercial model.
ZkSync announced Airbender Prime, a prover that Matter Labs says handled 99% of 7,200 consecutive Ethereum mainnet blocks in under 10 seconds each on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU.
The announcement came five days after Starknet said it is actively considering becoming an independent layer-1 (L1) blockchain, targeting full quantum resistance in 2027.
The two announcements answer the same deadline from opposite directions, since Ethereum's own target for L1 quantum resistance across execution, consensus, and data is December 2029.
A prover that meets the real-time benchmark
The Ethereum Foundation defines real-time proving as 99% of mainnet blocks proven in 10 seconds or less, which fits Ethereum's 12-second slot and propagation assumptions.
ZkSync's result maps to that definition, including witness preparation, with every block finishing in under 12 seconds.
Airbender Prime uses hash-based STARKs that combine GKR sumcheck, WHIR polynomial commitments, and BLAKE2s hashing, with Keccak-256-based commitments for L1 proofs replacing BN254 pairings.
Nvidia rates the card at 600 watts of board power, and marketplace reporting puts it near $16,000. The Foundation's target framework also covers proof sizes under 300 KiB, a long-term 128-bit security level, on-premise capital spending near $100,000, and power draw under 10 kilowatts.
Full-system electricity use, proof sizes and long-term operating costs for Prime await independent measurement, and the Foundation's public proving program continues to evaluate security and reliability.
One layer of the Ethereum quantum stack
Ethereum's ECDSA account signatures, BLS validator signatures and KZG data commitments belong to separate protocol-level work, and the December 2029 target stands as published, a schedule the Foundation calls aggressive. The prover operates outside Ethereum's consensus protocol.
Quantum preparation arrives while standalone chains struggle to pay their way. Blast set an Oct. 26 user-exit deadline, saying maintenance costs exceeded revenue, and Abstract is shutting down.
Aave's risk provider LlamaRisk recommended winding down V3 deployments on six chains, including zkSync, saying zkSync, Scroll and Sonic each generated less than $5,000 in quarterly protocol revenue at current balances.
The evidence points to consolidation and specialization, and many layer-2 (L2) blockchains keep operating. Cheap execution earns too little on its own, and liquidity, distribution, compliance, and institutional access are becoming the defensible layers.
Starknet's proving layer already rests on hash functions, according to StarkWare's June roadmap, with its Ethereum dependencies sitting in bridge messaging and blob data availability.
Becoming an L1 would bring those surfaces under Starknet's control and let it set its own timeline. The idea remains under consideration and would need governance approval and engineering execution.
ZkSync is investing in technology useful to Ethereum's own architecture and pointing its commercial effort at regulated finance. Starknet explores independence from the base layer, and zkSync builds components for it.
The bank pivot is documented
Matter Labs' third-quarter report says it prioritized private institutional interoperability over public Gateway interoperability.
Institutions building on its Prividium platform asked for private execution, direct Ethereum settlement, and atomic transfers between Prividium chains. The report removed the interop fees from the original public Gateway proposal and lists the private-interoperability fee model as ongoing work.
Matter Labs says Deutsche Bundesbank is testing Prividium's open-source permissioning engine in its own infrastructure, which lets regulated institutions run and inspect core code themselves.
The Cari case study from zkSync describes five founding US regional bank partners holding more than $8 trillion in assets. A zkSync-hosted summary puts the broader network at more than 30 institutions with over $10 trillion in combined assets.
Any link between Prividium usage and ZK token demand awaits a published fee model.
Where the Ethereum split goes from here
If Airbender Prime and similar systems keep meeting the Foundation's security, cost, proof-size, and on-premise targets, zkSync could supply proof infrastructure for Ethereum's route toward independently verifiable execution while Prividium pilots grow into fee-paying deployments.
That path gives former L2 teams a role as suppliers to the base layer and to regulated finance.
If Prividium deployments remain pilots, private-interoperability fees stay unfinished and public zkSync activity stays weak, the market reads zkSync as a prover stack with a technical result and a thin commercial one.
A compressed quantum timeline would add urgency to Starknet's L1 option and push Ethereum to accelerate its account, consensus, and data-layer migrations.
Ethereum's quantum preparations and its scaling sector are being restructured together, and each L2 team is picking among a sovereign chain, a supplier role to Ethereum, a bank-grade vendor business, or consolidation.
Ethereum is -3.22% over the past 24 hours and currently sits at rank #2 by market cap.

articles.title: Fed’s Williams sees AI supply squeeze lasting beyond 2 years
articles.text:
Fed’s Williams sees AI supply squeeze lasting beyond 2 years
New York Fed President John Williams’ comments came as he reaffirmed his view that the US Federal Reserve may need to raise interest rates once more this year.
New York Fed President John Williams said AI equipment supply could take more than two years to catch up with demand, which could add to inflationary pressure.
Williams made the comments during an interview with Bloomberg on Tuesday, saying that the buildout of AI infrastructure is pushing up chip prices and goods that use them.
Asked whether supply and demand within AI would become more balanced over the next two years, Williams said: “I think it’s going to take longer. Assuming the demand kind of impulse continues as expected, and that’s a big assumption.”
William’s comments came as he reaffirmed his view that the US Federal Reserve may need to raise interest rates once more this year as it seeks to lower inflation.
“I haven’t changed my view that it may be appropriate to have one more rate hike.”
However, Williams said “we’ll have to see” about 2027, saying “I don’t think at this time I have any reason to believe that we would need to do more.”
Meanwhile, Williams said he expects AI investment to stay strong even with higher rates.
“I think investors there are relatively price insensitive,” he said. “They feel that this is a huge, going to lead to huge productivity gains, huge transformative changes in our economy, and I think that happens not completely invariant to interest rates, but I don’t expect monetary policy to be really having a deep effect on that.”
Related: Anthropic strikes $9B compute deal with Bitcoin miner Riot: Report
An AI equipment supply shortage could have an impact on Bitcoin miners expanding into the sector, as they compete for chips and power equipment.
IREN signed $2.8 billion in new AI cloud contracts in July, while Cointelegraph reported on Monday that miners pursuing AI projects already face substantial financing requirements and increasingly selective lenders.

articles.title: Strive's new $500 million Bitcoin financing plan comes with a $257 million annual dividend problem
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Strive unveiled SATS, a new preferred stock carrying a fixed 15% annual dividend, to accelerate Bitcoin accumulation.
- Its $500 million financing model could fund nearly 4,700 BTC purchases, lifting total holdings to approximately 40,000 BTC.
- Annual preferred dividends could reach $257.4 million, leaving Strive dependent on fresh capital once its reserves run down.
Bitcoin treasury company Strive is introducing a second preferred-stock product to accelerate Bitcoin purchases beyond the limits of its existing financing strategy.
On Oct. 13, the company announced plans to offer five million shares of SATS, a perpetual preferred security with a fixed 15% annual dividend. At $100 per share, the firm would raise $500 million to support additional Bitcoin acquisitions.
The launch follows the rapid expansion of Strive's existing SATA preferred stock, whose outstanding stated amount has climbed from $200 million at its November 2025 debut to approximately $1.4 billion.
Strive's Bitcoin holdings have grown alongside that financing program, rising from 7,627 BTC at the beginning of 2026 to 35,595 BTC as of Oct. 14.
The new product comes as restrictions on SATA issuance constrain Strive's ability to raise capital. Management wants to expand Bitcoin purchases while prices remain below $100,000, but the additional financing could push its annual preferred-dividend obligations above $257 million.
Strive targets new investors as SATA financing faces limits
SATS will pay a fixed 15% annual dividend on a $100 stated amount, compared with SATA's variable 13%. Payments are scheduled every business day beginning Nov. 9, subject to board approval and available funds.
Unlike SATA, which targets a trading price around $100, SATS will have no comparable price-stability mechanism. The new shares will rank below SATA in Strive's capital structure but ahead of common equity.
Strive CEO Matt Cole said the company developed SATS after identifying demand from investors seeking predictable income and greater potential for capital appreciation.
Some existing SATA holders were concerned about possible reductions in its variable dividend, while institutional investors wanted more exposure to price appreciation.
The new structure also addresses a constraint on Strive's ability to raise capital.
According to Cole, SATA and Strategy's comparable STRC preferred stock have traded at or above their $100 stated amounts on fewer than 25% of trading days since their respective launches.
With Strive maintaining a policy against issuing SATA below $100, those trading patterns limit its ability to raise additional capital through the security.
Cole said the company needs “substantially more access to digital credit now” to expand its Bitcoin holdings at current prices.
SATS would let Strive pursue additional financing without SATA's issuance-price restriction, though the amount it can raise would still depend on investor demand.
New financing could add nearly 4,700 Bitcoin to Strive's treasury
Strive plans to use the additional financing capacity provided by SATS to accelerate its Bitcoin accumulation and increase potential returns for common shareholders.
Chief Risk Officer Jeff Walton said the company intends to achieve this through greater Bitcoin amplification, which measures outstanding preferred equity and debt at stated value relative to the market value of its Bitcoin holdings.
Strive is targeting an amplification ratio of 60% to 70% after the SATS launch, giving common shareholders greater exposure to Bitcoin price movements.
To illustrate the potential expansion, Strive's investor presentation models a $500 million SATS financing, with $387.5 million allocated to Bitcoin purchases and $112.5 million designated for an 18-month dividend reserve.
At an assumed Bitcoin price of $82,500, the purchases would add about 4,697 BTC to the company's treasury, bringing total holdings to about 40,000 BTC.
The company's preliminary prospectus states that it would fund the dividend reserve with existing cash and securities. Strive has also retained flexibility to direct offering proceeds toward income-generating assets, acquisitions, working capital, and share repurchases.
The strategy hinges on Bitcoin's appreciation exceeding the cost of preferred capital. Strive's internal model assumes the cryptocurrency will compound at 50% annually through 2030, compared with SATS's fixed 15% dividend.
However, the additional preferred capital would also magnify pressure on common shareholders during a sustained Bitcoin downturn, while dividend obligations continued to accumulate.
Strive faces $257 million annual dividend bill
The expansion would substantially increase Strive's recurring obligations to preferred shareholders.
A five-million-share SATS issuance would add $75 million in annual dividends. Combined with existing SATA payments, Strive's model puts the total at approximately $257.4 million a year, assuming SATA's variable rate remains at 13%.
Management plans to maintain approximately $386 million in cash and marketable securities as dividend reserves following the offering, enough to cover about 18 months of combined payments.
Chief Investment Officer Ben Werkman said the hypothetical post-offering balance sheet would contain approximately $3.56 billion in assets against $1.9 billion in preferred stated amounts.
The additional financing would increase asset coverage for senior SATA shares from 2.18 times to 2.54 times, while combined coverage for the two securities would stand at 1.87 times.
Strive's stress tests also show Bitcoin could fall to approximately $38,200 before its modeled total assets equaled the stated amount of outstanding preferred shares.
Werkman pointed to the company's lack of outstanding debt and its unencumbered Bitcoin holdings as protections against forced asset sales during market downturns.
However, the more immediate challenge is funding the dividends.
Bitcoin generates no recurring income, leaving Strive dependent on its cash reserves, asset sales, or fresh financing to sustain distributions.
The company acknowledges in its prospectus that it expects to fund cash dividends beyond the initial 18-month reserve period primarily through additional capital raising, including at-the-market securities offerings.
A prolonged Bitcoin decline could complicate that strategy by weakening demand for Strive's preferred and common shares just as its dividend obligations continue accumulating.
Missed preferred dividends would not automatically trigger a debt default, but unpaid amounts would accumulate and restrict distributions to junior shareholders.

articles.title: Bitwise CIO Sees ‘Crypto Spring’ in Q3 Market Rebound
articles.text:
Bitwise’s Hougan says Q3 charts point to ‘crypto spring’
Bitwise’s Matt Hougan said nearly every fundamental indicator that Bitwise tracks spiked sharply higher.
Bitwise chief investment officer Matt Hougan says Q3 may have been “one of the best quarters in crypto’s history,” arguing a sharp rebound in crypto prices and growing onchain markets point to the start of “crypto spring.”
In its quarterly market review published Thursday, Bitwise reported a 46.4% quarterly gain in its large-cap crypto index, along with $6 billion in US spot Bitcoin ETF inflows that brought year-to-date net flows back into positive territory.
The growth extended beyond the price of cryptocurrencies. The value of tokenized equities rose 65.5% to nearly $3.2 billion, while open interest on decentralized perpetual futures hit a new record near $26 billion, with a growing share tied to stocks, commodities, foreign exchange and pre-IPO shares.
“Page after page after page, it’s all the same: The most recent part of the chart is turning sharply upwards,” Hougan wrote. “That’s exactly what you want to see if you’re looking for the start of a crypto spring.”
Crypto analysts have been debating whether the market slump is finally over. CryptoQuant said in September that technical and onchain indicators confirmed a new Bitcoin bull market, while Bitget chief analyst Ryan Lee told Cointelegraph that more indicators were needed to confirm a cycle bottom. Hougan pointed to ETF flows and onchain activity as additional signs of a potential recovery.
10 large-cap crypto gain double digits
Bitcoin (BTC) gained 42.3% during Q3, while Ether (ETH) and Solana (SOL) rose 69.1% and 59.2%, respectively, according to Bitwise.
All 10 constituents of the firm’s large-cap crypto index posted double-digit quarterly gains, with Chainlink (LINK) the highest performer, climbing 97.6%.
“Three months ago, crypto was in the depths of despair,” said Hougan. “Prices, onchain activity, ETF flows—everything was down.”
Year-to-date performance of the assets tracked in the Bitwise 10 Large Cap Crypto Index. Source: Bitwise
However, the rebound did not extend to every corner of the industry.
Shares of Bitcoin miners Riot Platforms and Hut 8 fell 26.4% and 25.4%, respectively, during Q3, while Galaxy Digital dropped 16.8%, according to Bitwise.
The number of public companies holding Bitcoin fell almost 6% to 173 in the quarter, though their combined holdings grew 0.5%, while the number of public companies holding Ether fell to 35 from 40, even as their combined holdings increased.
Related: Crypto valuations could double as protocols link revenue to tokens: Bitwise CIO
Meanwhile, Bitwise’s large-cap crypto index remained down 6.2% for the year through September despite its strong quarterly gain.
Upcoming catalysts
Looking ahead, Bitwise said it expects the SEC’s innovation exemption to draw billions more of tokenized assets into blockchains.
“We believe Q4 moves tokenization from pilots to production. We expect the exemption will pull billions more of tokenized assets onto blockchains like Ethereum, Solana, NEAR, and others.”
Meanwhile, it expects the growing perpetual futures market to accelerate after more than $6 trillion was traded year-to-date across venues such as Hyperliquid and Lighter, up 42% from the same period a year earlier.
“With regulatory support expected this quarter, we project the growing perp market to accelerate as US investors start to arrive,” said Bitwise.

articles.title: HEX founder Richard Heart arrested with 'electronic devices' in Istanbul via Interpol warrant
articles.text:
Quick Take
- IHA reports Richard Heart and his wife were detained in Istanbul’s Beşiktaş district on October 14.
- An Interpol Red Notice requests provisional arrest, while countries decide how to act under their own laws.
- Heart’s separate SEC civil case was dismissed in February 2025; that ruling did not decide the Finnish suspicions.
Richard Heart, the founder of HEX and PulseChain, was reportedly detained with his wife in Istanbul on Oct. 14, according to İhlas News Agency (IHA). The agency linked the police operation to an Interpol Red Notice requested by Finland.
Heart, whose legal name is Richard James Schueler, and his wife, identified in the report as A.K., were taken into custody that morning in the Beşiktaş district, IHA said in an account carried by Daily Sabah. The reported operation took place at an address police had been monitoring.
The Finnish allegations date back to 2024. Yle reported that Finnish police suspected Schueler of gross tax evasion and assault, and that he had been remanded in custody in absentia on Sept. 13 that year. The decision was made without him being present, rather than following an arrest in Finland.
IHA said Istanbul police’s intelligence and financial-crimes units carried out the operation with support from Turkey’s National Intelligence Organization, MİT. Its account described technical and physical surveillance before officers moved in at the Beşiktaş address on Wednesday morning.
The agency reported seizures of cash, gold jewelry, watches and electronic devices, in an account carried by Star. It also listed three pistols and four long-barreled rifles, along with cash in U.S. dollars, euros and Turkish lira. These were reported search findings, not a determination of whether the seized property was linked to any offense.
INTERPOL’s Red Notice system asks national police to find and temporarily detain a wanted person while legal processes such as extradition or surrender are pursued. Countries decide how to act under their own laws. A Red Notice does not function as an international arrest warrant, and subjects sought for prosecution remain presumed innocent.
Heart previously faced a separate U.S. civil securities lawsuit. In its July 31, 2023 announcement, the SEC alleged that Heart, HEX, PulseChain and PulseX conducted unregistered crypto offerings raising more than $1 billion. The regulator also alleged that Heart and PulseChain diverted at least $12 million for luxury purchases.
Judge Carol Bagley Amon of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York granted dismissal on Feb. 28, 2025. The court found deficiencies in personal jurisdiction and the pleaded U.S. transactions or conduct, while giving the SEC an opportunity to amend its complaint. That ruling did not decide the Finnish suspicions.
IHA reported that the investigation concerning Schueler and his wife was continuing. Its account did not establish a completed extradition to Finland.

articles.title: Bitcoin Fog operator’s conviction upheld without Chainalysis disclosing source code
articles.text:
Quick Take
- The September 25 Bitcoin Fog appeal upheld Reactor-based testimony and affirmed Roman Sterlingov’s convictions and 150-month sentence.
- Source-code access failed on materiality and preservation grounds, while counsel and qualified experts could inspect Reactor’s heuristics.
- Reactor matched four of five known Bitcoin Fog addresses; a separate-case check covered 99.9% of a larger group.
The Bitcoin Fog appeal upheld expert testimony based on proprietary wallet tracing, with explained methods and corroboration supporting its admission. Roman Sterlingov’s effort to obtain the software’s source code failed on the record presented to the courts.
Blockchain analysis company Chainalysis drew attention to that result in October 13 commentary, presenting it as further validation of its Reactor software. The judgment itself came on September 25, when the D.C. Circuit affirmed Sterlingov’s convictions and 150-month sentence for operating Bitcoin Fog, a service that mixed users’ bitcoin to obscure transaction trails.
The decision matters because it explains how proprietary analysis became usable courtroom evidence and why this particular disclosure challenge failed. Its reasoning keeps three questions separate: whether expert testimony is reliable enough to admit, whether addresses have been attributed correctly, and what that evidence establishes about a person.
How the court assessed wallet tracing
Under Federal Rule of Evidence 702, the party offering a qualified expert must demonstrate, more likely than not, that the testimony will help the fact-finder, rests on sufficient facts or data, uses reliable principles and methods, and reflects a reliable application of those methods to the case.
Daubert supplies considerations for that reliability inquiry, including testing, peer review, known or potential error rates, and general acceptance. The appeals court explained that these considerations are flexible and nonexhaustive.
The appellate posture also matters. The panel reviewed admission of the testimony for abuse of discretion, recognizing the trial judge’s latitude both in deciding how to assess reliability and in reaching a reliability determination.
FBI witness Luke Scholl and Chainalysis analyst Elizabeth Bisbee testified that Reactor clustered and attributed more than 900,000 Bitcoin addresses to Bitcoin Fog.
The opinion describes three kinds of clustering heuristics, or inference rules. Co-spend clustering treats addresses used together as transaction inputs as being controlled by one person or entity. Behavioral clustering looks for matching transaction patterns, including change-address behavior and digital fingerprints. Intelligence-based clustering adds information from sources such as data leaks, court documents and data partnerships.
The prosecution’s case also contained evidence beyond clustering. The opinion recounts IP-overlap analysis, Sterlingov’s earlier activity concerning mixers and darknet promotion, financial records, and Bitcoin Fog’s cessation of operations shortly after his arrest.
What the checks actually showed
Both Reactor witnesses acknowledged that the software had not been peer-reviewed and that they did not know its error rate. The panel nevertheless found other markers of reliability: the witnesses’ experience, comparisons with information obtained later through legal processes, use by law enforcement and private-sector specialists, explanations of the methods, and corroboration.
Two checks deserve particular care. First, the opinion cites a government contractor’s confirmation that Reactor correctly clustered and attributed 99.9% of a large group of addresses in another case. The opinion supplies that percentage without a complete public sampling design. Its stated scope is those addresses in that other case; using it as a product-wide error rate would expand the result beyond that scope.
Second, Scholl checked five known addresses used by Bitcoin Fog during the government’s undercover transactions. Reactor’s Bitcoin Fog cluster contained four. Sterlingov characterized the result as a 20% error rate, but the panel accepted the trial court’s explanation that Reactor was conservative and underinclusive for the purposes of this case.
Missing a known service address and wrongly assigning an unrelated address to that service are different errors.
A separate empirical study illustrates the value of comparing attribution with known service data. The 2025 Ghost Clusters paper compared Chainalysis attribution with seized-wallet data from BestMixer, Hansa Market and Wall Street Market. It found conservative coverage and few but nonzero false positives, with coverage varying across services and their historical periods.
The researchers compared attribution snapshots across the three services’ historical periods. The paper appeared after Sterlingov’s 2024 trial.
Why the source-code challenge failed
The district court ordered Reactor’s heuristics and underlying assumptions made available to Sterlingov’s counsel and qualified experts under a protective order. It restricted Sterlingov’s personal access because of concerns that the information could help someone circumvent tracing techniques. The panel also noted that Sterlingov’s experts had refused to review the disclosures regardless of the protective order’s scope.
Access to those materials was distinct from access to the program’s source code. The appellate opinion says the district court repeatedly asked Sterlingov to explain why the code was material and relevant to his defense. He did not provide that explanation. The panel also noted that the trial court had displayed willingness to provide the code if the need was justified.
The constitutional arguments faced additional appellate limits. The constitutional objections newly advanced over access to the full software, including code, received plain-error review because they had not been raised below. A previously raised objection concerned Sterlingov’s personal access to the heuristic material. The panel distinguished the two, while saying the constitutional claims were unpersuasive under either discussed standard.
The Confrontation Clause argument also failed. The panel rejected the theory that the machine-generated outputs required source-code disclosure under the right to confront witnesses. Even if it accepted Sterlingov’s argument that human programming judgments made the outputs an inference from a human-designed model, it said that would not require production of the code on the facts presented.
Due process involved both forfeiture and an alternative substantive conclusion. Sterlingov’s opening appellate brief did not contest denial of the Rule 17(c) subpoena request, so the panel found that challenge and due-process claims bound up with it forfeited. It also rejected an independent due-process theory because he had not shown a material impairment of his defense.
Which inference the evidence must support
The older research helps explain why service attribution and personal ownership need separate treatment. Sarah Meiklejohn and colleagues’ 2013 Bitcoin clustering paper distinguished control of an address from ownership of customer funds: a wallet service can control addresses holding money owned by different users.
The paper also warned that its change-address heuristic could make incorrect links that merge unrelated clusters, particularly as transaction behavior changes.
Evidence naming a service has a different job from evidence identifying its operator or establishing a customer’s ownership.
The evidence rules retain a route for probing an expert’s basis. Rule 705 allows an expert to state an opinion without first setting out the underlying facts or data unless the court orders otherwise, but permits requiring disclosure of those facts or data on cross-examination.
The practical lesson from Sterlingov is therefore specific. Explained methods, corroboration and protected access to methodology can support admission of proprietary tracing testimony. In this case, the failure to explain the code’s material connection to the defense and the way the objections were raised helped defeat the disclosure challenge.

articles.title: Bitcoin plunges to $81,300 support as Fed hike odds hit 55% amid $100 million crypto wipeout
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin fell below $83,000 after hotter US inflation triggered more than $100 million in crypto liquidations within an hour.
- October Fed rate hike odds surged from 21% to 55%, threatening Bitcoin's recovery as Treasury yields climbed.
- Bitcoin now faces an $81,300 support test, with further losses possible if bond yields and the dollar keep rising.
Bitcoin fell below $83,000 on Wednesday as hotter-than-expected US core inflation data revived expectations of further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, triggering a fresh wave of liquidations across the cryptocurrency market.
CoinGlass data showed that over $100 million in leveraged positions were liquidated in the hour after the inflation report was released. This also pushed total liquidations above $220 million over 24 hours.
The sharp increase in forced selling highlighted how quickly traders reacted to renewed inflation pressures and the prospect of tighter US monetary policy.
Hot inflation revives Fed rate hike bets and rattles bond markets
According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, consumer prices increased 3.7% annually in September, above the 3.6% forecast and August's 3.4% reading. Headline consumer prices rose 0.6% during the month, matching expectations, while core prices increased 0.3%, above the 0.2% consensus estimate.
On an annual basis, core inflation accelerated to 2.6% from 2.4%, suggesting that underlying price pressures remain persistent even after excluding volatile food and energy costs. This marks the 67th consecutive month US inflation has stayed above the Fed's 2% target.
Energy remained the biggest contributor to inflation, reflecting the economic fallout from the ongoing US-Iran conflict. Gasoline prices surged 9.1% during September, accounting for more than half the increase in headline CPI, while the broader energy index climbed 5.2%.
However, inflationary pressures spread to other parts of the economy. Shelter costs increased 0.4%, used vehicle prices climbed 0.7%, and higher prices were also recorded for recreation, education, air travel and medical services.
The breadth of these increases complicated expectations that policymakers could look past an energy-driven inflation shock without additional tightening.
Bond markets reacted sharply, with the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield reversing an earlier decline to rise approximately 7 to 9 basis points during the session.
Robin Brooks, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, warned that the inflation figures risked reigniting instability across global bond markets after a period of relative calm.
Meanwhile, the repricing also spread to expectations for Federal Reserve policy. Kalshi's prediction market showed the probability of a 25-basis-point Fed hike in October rising to 55% from 21%, while traders increased bets on further tightening through 2027.
Notably, the Fed had previously raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points in September to a target range of 3.75% to 4%, its first increase in more than three years.
Can-Luca Köymen, investment strategist at Sygnum Bank, told CryptoSlate that the stronger inflation reading had reopened the possibility of another increase this month, although the bank still expects policymakers to hold rates steady.
“Core at 0.3%, above consensus, puts an October hike back in play after the market had faded it to one in five,” Köymen said.
He noted that the Fed's preferred inflation measure, the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, will not be released until the day after its October policy decision, leaving officials to assess inflation risks without the latest PCE figures.
For Bitcoin, the immediate concern is that higher Treasury yields increase the appeal of interest-bearing assets, while a stronger dollar can tighten financial conditions and weaken demand for speculative investments.
Köymen said these macroeconomic pressures would likely influence Bitcoin's near-term direction more than daily flows into spot exchange-traded funds.
Bitcoin's demand recovery faces a critical test
The renewed macroeconomic pressure arrived just as Bitcoin's underlying demand indicators were showing signs of improvement following two months of weakness.
According to CryptoQuant data, spot Bitcoin demand has begun to recover alongside continued growth in futures demand, creating a market structure similar to that seen in August.
The analytics platform estimated that total demand increased by about 69,000 BTC after two largely negative months, suggesting buying activity was strengthening beyond leveraged derivatives positions.
This combination has historically accompanied bullish phases in Bitcoin's market cycle, when stronger purchases of the underlying asset help sustain price advances supported by futures traders.
The improving demand picture offered a potential foundation for Bitcoin's recovery after repeated attempts to establish support above $80,000.
However, Wednesday's inflation shock introduced a fresh challenge.
The latest liquidations followed an earlier wave of more than $800 million in forced position closures across the cryptocurrency market, raising concerns that leveraged traders remained exposed despite the recent reduction in risk.
Before the inflation report, Ryan Lee, chief analyst at Bitget Research, had warned that the market's previous liquidation wave might not have fully cleared excessive leverage.
He pointed to elevated open interest as a potential source of renewed instability if an unexpectedly strong inflation reading pushed Treasury yields higher and forced investors to reassess the Fed's interest rate trajectory.
That concern has grown more pressing after Wednesday's selloff, as the latest liquidation figures suggest leveraged traders remain vulnerable to sudden macroeconomic developments.
Lewis Huang, an analyst at Bitget, told CryptoSlate that $81,300 is Bitcoin's immediate support level, warning that a sustained decline below that threshold could expose the asset to further losses.
He said the risk would increase if falling cryptocurrency prices coincided with further gains in Treasury yields, dollar strength and deteriorating sentiment across other risk assets.
Still, CryptoQuant's improving spot demand figures suggest the market may have some capacity to absorb selling pressure if underlying buying activity continues to expand.
The distinction will become increasingly important if investors respond to the inflation surprise by reducing exposure to leveraged positions while longer-term buyers continue accumulating Bitcoin.
The next major test comes at the Federal Reserve's Oct. 27–28 policy meeting, followed by the September PCE inflation release on Oct. 29.
Until then, Bitcoin's ability to defend the $81,300 support level will help determine whether improving spot demand can withstand another round of monetary tightening expectations.
Bitcoin is -1.90% over the past 24 hours and currently sits at rank #1 by market cap.

articles.title: Ca sĩ Đông Hùng: Tôi thích học cách làm mới mình
articles.text:
Biến áp lực thành động lực
Từ các sự kiện A50, A80, đến hiện tại là chương trình "Anh trai vượt ngàn chông gai", bình luận "thời của Đông Hùng tới rồi" khiến anh vui hay áp lực nhiều hơn?
Với tôi, "thời" là lúc mình được khán giả "nhìn thấy". Có khán giả là có thời, nên tôi luôn cố gắng trên mọi sân khấu mình có cơ hội biểu diễn. Áp lực thì luôn có, nhưng là những áp lực tích cực. Khi mọi người dành kỳ vọng, tôi càng có động lực muốn làm tốt hơn.
Tôi xúc động khi các ca khúc truyền cảm hứng yêu nước mình thể hiện trong dịp kỷ niệm A50, A80 được khán giả ủng hộ nồng nhiệt.
Với "Anh trai vượt ngàn chông gai", sau một khoảng thời gian rất lâu, tôi mới quyết định tham gia lại chương trình truyền hình thực tế. Tôi đã từng nghĩ mình không phù hợp. Nhưng cũng chính điều đó khiến tôi muốn thử sức bản thân.
Đến khi tham gia, tôi rất thích và cảm thấy thoải mái với môi trường mà chương trình tạo ra. Các bạn trẻ cho tôi thấy rất nhiều năng lượng và cách làm mới, nhiều sáng tạo và không ngại những thử thách mới. Tôi học được từ các bạn ấy rất nhiều điều.
Suốt hành trình vừa qua, Đông Hùng tìm kiếm điều gì từ "Anh trai vượt ngàn chông gai"?
Chương trình mang lại cho tôi nhiều cảm xúc bất ngờ. Tôi muốn được làm việc với những nghệ sĩ rất khác, thử những điều trước đây chưa từng làm. Với tôi, đó là một hành trình để khám phá chính mình.
Trước đây tôi thường muốn mọi thứ phải thật chắc chắn mới bước lên sân khấu. Nhưng chương trình cho tôi hiểu rằng đôi khi mình phải dám thử, dám đặt mình vào những hoàn cảnh không quen thuộc.
Thay đổi không có nghĩa là đánh mất mình
Và khi tham gia "Anh trai vượt ngàn chông gai", anh được làm những điều từ rất lâu rồi mình không làm?
Đúng vậy, đây là điều tôi thấy mãn nguyện.
Tôi không phải người quá ồn ào, thích sự đơn giản và những cuộc trò chuyện có chiều sâu. Nhưng kể từ khi tiếp xúc với anh em trong chương trình, tôi cảm thấy mình thả lỏng và thoải mái hơn.
Tôi nghĩ phiên bản Đông Hùng của "Anh trai vượt ngàn chông gai" là một phiên bản giúp tôi được trở về đúng với tuổi trẻ của mình.
Khán giả và thị trường kỳ vọng ngày một nhiều hơn, anh có nghĩ mình cần thay đổi để phù hợp?
Tôi thích học cách làm mới mình, thử những màu sắc âm nhạc khác và tiếp cận nhiều đối tượng khán giả. Nhưng thay đổi không có nghĩa là đánh mất mình. Thị trường thay đổi mình phải chuyển động, còn cốt lõi của mình tôi vẫn muốn giữ.
Tôi mong rằng các bạn Đồng Hương (cộng đồng người hâm mộ của Đông Hùng) và những khán giả yêu thương sẽ luôn dõi theo con đường làm nghề của tôi. Tôi nghĩ vậy là đủ. Không cần nghĩ là "thời tới" hay "thời qua". Tôi có khán giả của mình, mình phục vụ khán giả của mình, vậy là đủ rồi.
Trân trọng mái ấm gia đình
Bà xã đồng hành với anh thế nào trong giai đoạn bận rộn này?
Vợ là người giúp tôi giữ được sự ổn định. Tôi may mắn khi có vợ và ê kíp do vợ xây dựng luôn đồng hành trên mọi hành trình. Những thứ khán giả nhìn thấy trên sân khấu là thành quả của rất nhiều đầu việc phía sau.
Vì vậy, vợ không đứng sau sự nghiệp của tôi, mà đồng hành với tôi trong cả cuộc sống. Tôi nghĩ, sự nghiệp của người đàn ông không chỉ là đạt được những thành tựu trong công việc, mà bên cạnh đó gia đình cũng là một sự nghiệp đáng tự hào. Mái ấm gia đình vô cùng quan trọng. Bà xã đã ở bên tôi từ những lúc khó khăn nhất, nên cô ấy hiểu hành trình này hơn ai hết. Tôi may mắn có một người như vậy song hành cùng mình.
Từ khi có gia đình, tôi cũng rèn cho mình nếp sống chỉn chu, trưởng thành hơn. Vợ cũng là người giúp tôi nhận ra được rất nhiều thiếu sót, sau đó chỉnh dần, sửa dần, dù mất khá nhiều thời gian để tôi hình thành những thói quen mới (cười).
Cuộc sống thường ngày ở gia đình của anh thế nào?
Cuộc sống của tôi ở nhà khá bình thường, đôi lúc có chút… nhạt (cười). Có những ngày hai vợ chồng đi về làm muộn, bé Mặp và bà ngoại đã ngủ. Có những ngày được ở nhà thì đưa con đi học, chơi với con.
Tôi thích những khoảnh khắc rất nhỏ như thế. Rời ánh đèn sân khấu, được về nhà, ăn bữa cơm cùng gia đình, nghe con kể những chuyện trong ngày… lúc đó tôi cảm thấy mình được trở về đúng với mình nhất.
Tôi và bà xã có những điểm giống nhau nhưng chắc chắn cũng có những lúc khác quan điểm. Tôi nghĩ điều quan trọng không phải là ai đúng, ai phải nhường ai, mà là cuối cùng cả hai cùng thống nhất được điều gì là tốt nhất.
Trong việc nuôi dạy con, anh muốn con thấy ở bố điều gì?
Bố mẹ nào cũng muốn con cái tự hào về mình. Vì vậy, mọi thứ chúng tôi làm bây giờ chỉ muốn con mình có một môi trường học tập tốt, một cuộc sống tốt. Tôi muốn sau này, con sẽ thấy được bố mẹ là những người có ích, muốn con trở thành người tử tế và biết rung động trước những điều đẹp đẽ xung quanh.
Con từng hát song ca cùng anh trên sóng VTV và được nhiều khán giả yêu mến. Nếu một ngày con muốn nối nghiệp bố, anh có ủng hộ không?
Nếu con thực sự yêu âm nhạc và muốn theo nghề, tôi sẽ ủng hộ, nhưng không bao giờ bắt con phải nối nghiệp bố.
Nếu một ngày con nói muốn trở thành ca sĩ, điều đầu tiên tôi dặn con sẽ là: "Con phải yêu việc mình làm trước". Nghề này có ánh đèn, có những khoảnh khắc rất đẹp, nhưng phía sau đó là rất nhiều năm tháng tập luyện, thất vọng và cả những lúc không ai nhìn thấy mình. Dù con có chọn con đường nào, vợ chồng tôi cũng luôn có mặt ở đó cùng con.
Anh có nghĩ mình là người chồng, người cha như vợ và con kỳ vọng?
Thật khó để trả lời câu hỏi này, tôi chỉ biết cố gắng từng ngày. Vai trò người chồng, người cha là một vai trò tôi luôn tự hào!
Cảm ơn anh!
Đông Hùng sinh năm 1993, từng là ca sĩ triển vọng của Sao mai Điểm hẹn 2012 và Top 3 của Vietnam Idol 2013. Anh được yêu mến bởi giọng hát trong, khỏe khoắn, ngoại hình sáng.
Năm 2017, Đông Hùng từng chia sẻ về cuộc sống lao đao vì giúp mẹ trả nợ chục tỷ đồng. Hiện tại, ca sĩ cho biết cuộc sống ổn định nên không muốn nhắc về biến cố cũ.

articles.title: Gia Lai yêu cầu chấn chỉnh tình trạng nhiều địa phương vắng tập huấn phòng, chống thiên tai
articles.text:
TPO - Việc tham gia các lớp tập huấn nâng cao năng lực cho cán bộ làm công tác phòng, chống thiên tai cấp xã năm 2026 tại một số địa phương ở tỉnh Gia Lai chưa nghiêm túc, nhiều xã tham gia chưa đủ số lượng, có xã đăng ký nhưng không tham dự.
Ngày 14/10, UBND tỉnh Gia Lai cho biết, đã có yêu cầu các xã, phường chấn chỉnh việc tham gia tập huấn công tác phòng, chống thiên tai.
Trước đó, trong các ngày 17-18/9, Sở Nông nghiệp và Môi trường tỉnh Gia Lai tổ chức 2 lớp tập huấn công tác phòng, chống thiên tai cho 58 xã, phường khu vực phía Đông tỉnh.
Gia Lai là một trong những địa phương chịu thiệt hại nặng nề do thiên tai năm 2025.
Nội dung tập huấn tập trung các quy định chức năng, nhiệm vụ của UBND cấp xã về công tác phòng, chống thiên tai; hướng dẫn triển khai Nghị định số 09/2025/NĐ-CP về chính sách hỗ trợ sản xuất nông nghiệp để khôi phục sản xuất vùng bị thiệt hại do thiên tai, dịch hại thực vật; một số nội dung liên quan đến quỹ phòng, chống thiên tai.
Đồng thời, hướng dẫn lập, triển khai phương án ứng phó thiên tai, củng cố đội xung kích phòng, chống thiên tai cấp xã; hệ thống cảnh báo sớm thiên tai và hướng dẫn khai thác, sử dụng hệ thống quan trắc mưa, mực nước tự động chuyên dùng trong công tác phòng, chống thiên tai; hướng dẫn cập nhật dữ liệu và khai thác, sử dụng phần mềm hệ thống thông tin phòng, chống thiên tai tỉnh.
Theo yêu cầu, mỗi xã, phường cử 3 người tham gia tập huấn. Qua thống kê có 57/58 xã, phường đăng ký đủ từ 3 người trở lên; 1 địa phương đăng ký 2 người. Tổng số đăng ký là 179 người, đạt 102,9% so với số lượng theo yêu cầu (174 người). Tuy nhiên, thực tế chỉ có 141 người tham gia, vắng 38 người.
Đặc biệt, có 4 đơn vị đã đăng ký nhưng không có người tham gia, gồm phường Quy Nhơn Bắc, xã Vĩnh Sơn, phường An Nhơn Bắc và xã Ân Tường.
Ngoài ra, có 5 đơn vị tham gia 1 người, gồm phường Quy Nhơn Tây, xã Nhơn Châu, xã An Vinh, phường Tam Quan, phường Hoài Nhơn Bắc.
Chủ tịch UBND tỉnh Gia Lai yêu cầu UBND các xã, phường nêu trên chỉ đạo chấn chỉnh việc cử cán bộ tham gia các lớp tập huấn về công tác phòng, chống thiên tai; bảo đảm bố trí cán bộ tham gia đầy đủ, đúng thành phần, đúng thời gian theo yêu cầu, không để tái diễn tình trạng vắng mặt hoặc tham gia không đủ số lượng.
TPO - Dự báo từ 15-25/10, miền Bắc chưa có dấu hiệu xuất hiện không khí lạnh, nền nhiệt cao dự báo duy trì liên tục. Nam Bộ chiều nay có mưa dông rải rác. Các khu vực khác trời nắng, ít mưa.
TPO - Sau gần 10 năm chờ đợi, hình hài cây cầu vượt tại nút giao đường Phạm Tu - đường 70 đã dần lộ diện khi các trụ cầu hoàn thiện và nhiều nhịp dầm liên tục đang được đổ bê tông, hướng tới mục tiêu hoàn thành trước ngày 31/12.
TPO - Một nhóm chat, vài tấm ảnh chế, hàng loạt lời giễu cợt có thể đẩy một người trẻ vào những ngày mất ngủ, hoảng loạn và tự cô lập. Khi mạng xã hội trở thành nơi bắt nạt, ai sẽ giúp các em thoát khỏi vòng xoáy tổn thương? Làm thế nào để mạng xã hội không trở thành nơi bào mòn cảm xúc và phá vỡ những mối quan hệ?
TPO - Ông Nguyễn Hồng Diên - Ủy viên Ban Chấp hành Trung ương Đảng, Phó Chủ tịch Quốc hội tiếp xúc với cử tri 13 xã, phường phía Tây tỉnh Gia Lai trước kỳ họp thứ 2, Quốc hội khóa XVI.
TPO - Thiếu tướng Trần Văn Lượng - Phó Tư lệnh, Tham mưu trưởng Cảnh sát biển Việt Nam, yêu cầu Bộ Tư lệnh Vùng Cảnh sát biển 4 tăng cường các biện pháp nghiệp vụ, nắm chắc tình hình tội phạm, vi phạm pháp luật trên biển; quyết liệt ngăn chặn tàu cá khai thác hải sản bất hợp pháp, không báo cáo, không theo quy định.
TPO - Tây Ninh xây dựng đề án thành lập thành phố trực thuộc Trung ương, dự kiến trình Bộ Chính trị xin chủ trương, trong bối cảnh kinh tế tăng trưởng 10,3%.
TPO - Phó trưởng Ban Tổ chức Trung ương Hà Minh Hải vừa ký ban hành hướng dẫn một số nội dung về vị trí việc làm công chức, viên chức, bản mô tả công việc, khung năng lực và cơ cấu ngạch công chức trong các cơ quan của Đảng, MTTQ Việt Nam và các tổ chức chính trị - xã hội.
TPO - Một vụ nổ nghi có liên quan đến pháo xảy ra chiều 14/10 tại nhà dân ở thôn Bát Trang, xã An Trường (Hải Phòng) khiến 2 người thương nặng, phải nhập viện cấp cứu.
TPO - Kết luận của Ban Chấp hành Trung ương nêu rõ, việc xác định phạm vi, mức độ, nội dung sửa đổi, bổ sung Điều lệ Đảng phải căn cứ vào kết quả tổng kết thực tiễn và nghiên cứu lý luận; không ấn định trước nội dung sửa đổi, bổ sung, đồng thời không né tránh những vấn đề mới đặt ra.
Dọc tuyến đường hơn 40km, từ xã Thanh Thủy đến Nghĩa trang liệt sĩ quốc gia Vị Xuyên, hàng trăm người đã đội nắng tiễn đưa 93 hài cốt liệt sĩ về nơi an nghỉ cuối cùng.
TPO - Ủy ban Kiểm tra Trung ương đề nghị Ban Bí thư xem xét, thi hành kỷ luật ông Sử Ngọc Anh, nguyên: Thành ủy viên, Phó Bí thư Đảng ủy, Phó Giám đốc Sở KH&ĐT TPHCM.
TPO - Ngày 14/10, Đoàn công tác của Chính phủ do Phó Thủ tướng Chính phủ Nguyễn Văn Thắng làm Trưởng đoàn đã có buổi làm việc với lãnh đạo thành phố Bắc Ninh về tình hình triển khai thực hiện các giải pháp thúc đẩy mục tiêu tăng trưởng kinh tế hai con số.
TPO - Vụ cháy tại nhà kho công ty thủy sản và sản xuất nước mắm trong khu công nghiệp ở xã Lương Thế Trân, tỉnh Cà Mau được cơ quan chức năng bước đầu xác định do chập điện.
TPO - Gần 60 năm sau ngày chứng kiến các liệt sĩ bị vùi lấp trong các rãnh chôn tập thể, ông Võ Huy Thịnh, một trong số các nhân chứng tìm đến Công viên văn hóa Lê Thị Riêng từ sớm, ngậm ngùi thắp hương tiễn đưa các anh về nơi an nghỉ cuối cùng.

articles.title: Chồng mất vì tai nạn, vợ nghèo gồng gánh nuôi con
articles.text:
Bươn chải mưu sinh
Tiếp chúng tôi trong căn nhà nhỏ vừa mới xây, còn chưa kịp sơn tại thôn Tú Sơn, xã Mường Động, tỉnh Phú Thọ, chị Nguyễn Hồng Nhung (SN 1985) vẫn chưa nguôi nỗi đau sau khi chồng mình là anh Bùi Văn Phương ra đi mãi mãi cách đây 8 tháng.
Chị Nhung kể, hôm xảy ra vụ việc là khoảng 5h chiều. Khi đó, anh Phương vừa đi làm thuê về, chỉ kịp tắm qua rồi lấy xe máy sang nhà chủ gần đó lấy tiền công. Di chuyển cách nhà gần 1km thì anh Phương gặp tai nạn, tử vong tại chỗ.
"Lúc đó, tôi đang bán hàng ở chợ thì được báo tin chồng gặp tai nạn. Tôi tức tốc đến nơi, cầu mong đó không phải chồng mình. Nhưng đến khi nhìn thấy biển số xe máy của chồng, tôi ngất đi, không biết gì nữa, tỉnh lại thì đã thấy đang ở nhà", chị Nhung kể.
Lo hậu sự cho chồng xong, chị phải mất rất nhiều thời gian để ổn định tâm lý. Được gia đình và bạn bè động viên, đến giờ chị nguôi ngoai phần nào, cố gắng tiếp tục chạy chợ để kiếm tiền nuôi các con ăn học.
"Anh Phương là người chồng thứ hai, tôi với anh có 3 đứa con, 2 gái, 1 trai. Cháu lớn năm nay 8 tuổi, cháu thứ hai 6 tuổi và con trai út mới 4 tuổi. Tôi còn đang nuôi hai cháu là con với chồng trước, trong đó có một cháu 15 tuổi bị bệnh bẩm sinh", chị Nhung chia sẻ về các con của mình.
Từ khi chồng mất, ngoài việc bán hàng ở chợ, chị Nhung tranh thủ đưa các mặt hàng lên mạng bán online. Nhiều người biết hoàn cảnh của chị nên thường xuyên đặt hàng ủng hộ. Tuy nhiên, lời lãi cũng không nhiều, trong khi mọi chi phí sinh hoạt, học hành của các con đều dồn lên vai chị.
Gia cảnh khó khăn
Bà Bùi Thị Lý (SN 1969, mẹ chồng chị Nhung) chia sẻ: "Nhiều hôm con dâu đi bán hàng về muộn mà lòng tôi cũng nóng như lửa đốt, lo lắng và thương con vất vả. Tôi ốm đau liên miên nên chỉ đỡ đần việc cơm nước.
Thương các cháu mất bố khi còn quá nhỏ. Đứa út nhiều hôm chỉ lên bàn thờ rồi hồn nhiên hỏi "Sao bố cháu ngủ lâu vậy bà?", những lúc đó tôi chỉ biết ứa nước mắt, không biết nói gì", bà Lý nghẹn ngào.
Sống gần nhà chị Nhung, bà Bùi Thị Chỉ (65 tuổi) cho biết: "Hoàn cảnh nhà cháu Nhung rất éo le, giờ một mình phải gồng gánh nuôi 5 đứa con. Hàng xóm thương tình nhưng cũng chẳng thể giúp được gì nhiều".
Ông Bùi Minh Chiến, Trưởng thôn Tú Sơn cũng chia sẻ, gia đình chị Nhung là hộ cận nghèo, sau khi anh Phương mất vì tai nạn giao thông, cuộc sống càng khó khăn hơn.
"Thời điểm xảy ra sự việc, người dân trong thôn người góp gạo, người góp tiền để hỗ trợ gia đình lo hậu sự. Chúng tôi luôn động viên chị Nhung cố gắng để nuôi dạy các cháu nên người", ông Chiến nói và bày tỏ mong muốn các nhà hảo tâm chia sẻ với hoàn cảnh hiện tại, chung tay hỗ trợ giúp đỡ để gia đình chị Nhung sớm ổn định cuộc sống, các cháu nhỏ không dang dở học hành.
Mọi sự giúp đỡ gia đình chị Nguyễn Hồng Nhung, xin độc giả và các nhà hảo tâm có thể gửi về số tài khoản của chị Nhung: 5503041985, Ngân hàng VPBank.
Hoặc gửi qua Chương trình Chung tay vì ATGT của Báo Xây dựng, số tài khoản: 115000106087, Ngân hàng TMCP Công thương Việt Nam - Chi nhánh Hà Nội. (Nội dung ghi rõ: Ủng hộ chị Nhung ở Phú Thọ).
