articles.title: Flock CEO: We haven't 'fired' any police departments as customers | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Flock CEO Garrett Langley said that his company has not ended any contracts with its customers over abuse of its products.
Speaking to TechCrunch editor-in-chief Connie Loizos at the Disrupt 2026 conference in San Francisco, Langley responded to criticisms facing the company about the misuse of its license plate reader cameras by police departments. It comes after streams of reporting identifying dozens of police officers who have been arrested, fired, or told to resign after being caught abusing access to Flock’s nationwide database of license plate detections, oftentimes to stalk people without permission.
Langley told Loizos that the company would end a relationship with a customer where there was clear widespread abuse of its systems. But, the CEO said, it has not to date “fired” a customer, as he put it, such as a police department or law enforcement agency. Langley said Flock had the debate internally, but argued that the company should not take away its product from a community that might need it in its efforts to fight crime.
“If a customer knowingly broke the law, we would fire them immediately. That’s very easy,” Langley said.
“Most of the debate is nuanced into ‘what if two officers out of fifty were caught?’ Today, we haven’t fired any customers, but it’s not off the table in the case of some pretty drastic law-abiding issue,” added Langley.
The abuse of Flock’s systems and the data it collects is the latest in an array of controversies embroiling the Atlanta, Georgia-based maker of license plate reader cameras. Flock has more than 100,000 cameras around the United States, which allow local police departments and federal agencies to track the whereabouts of vehicle license plates and people as they pass by.
By allowing its law enforcement customers to track license plates outside of their jurisdictions, some police departments can track cars across the entire country through Flock’s national central database.
Protest outside Disrupt during Flock interview
Flock has become a flashpoint in the surveillance debate, prompting towns, cities, and communities to reject the company’s cameras by canceling their contracts or allowing them to expire, citing privacy fears.
There have been multiple reports of Flock reactivating cameras against their customers’ wishes, prompting local residents to tape trash bags over the cameras and other times destroying them.
While Langley spoke on the Disrupt stage, demonstrators gathered outside the venue to protest against Flock’s AI-powered surveillance, wearing costumes like the red robes from “The Handmaid’s Tale” and cardboard replicas of Flock cameras on their heads, while clips from the “1984” movie played on a loudspeaker behind them. Others carried signs declaring “Flock off,” or “Flock = ICE.”
Flock does not have a direct contract with the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), but the agency has reportedly accessed Flock data in the past by collaborating with local police departments that use Flock cameras.
Ashley Ortiz, an organizer with local progressive activist group The Wolves, told TechCrunch that she wants local lawmakers to take constituents’ concerns about Flock more seriously.
“I think Flock is going to be the start of a lot more community building, because we can come together around something as bipartisan as not enjoying mass surveillance,” said Ortiz. “We have Republicans who join us, conservatives who agree, we have sovereign citizens cutting down Flock cameras, so it’s not just the left who doesn’t want AI-powered mass surveillance.”
When asked what questions she has for Langley, Ortiz said, “What about AI-powered mass surveillance should be making us feel safe?”
In answer to that, Langley argued, onstage, that its license plate tracking system has been allowing police departments to solve more crimes and to solve them faster. He offered anecdotes, such as a stolen car with a baby in the back seat being found quickly thanks, he said, to Flock systems.
Still, Flock has also faced criticism for cybersecurity issues, and camera accuracy issues that have resulted in dozens of police stops and wrongful arrests, including a journalist who was driving a review vehicle.
Some communities have replaced their Flock contracts with rival surveillance companies, such as Axon, the maker of Taser weapons and police bodycams.
On a potential sale to Axon, Langley said the company was not considering a sale. “No, we’ve no desire to sell the company.”

articles.title: Sony is taking on DJI with its new ECM-W5 wireless microphone kit - Engadget
articles.text:
Sony is taking on DJI with its new ECM-W5 wireless microphone kit
The kit includes two transmitters and a receiver, and it supports 32-bit float recording.
Sony has announced the ECM-W5, a $400 wireless microphone kit that's clearly designed to be as easy to use as DJI's affordable wireless mics, provided creators are willing to pay a comparatively premium price to use it. The ECM-W5 combines wireless transmitters and a receiver that can directly record to a Sony camera (or other devices over USB-C), capturing 96kHz audio from up to 500 meters away in line-of-sight conditions.
The ECM-W5 is easiest to use with Sony's Alpha series cameras, where it can connect over the Multi Interface Shoe (Sony's modern answer to the hotshoe) to receive power and transfer data. A kit only comes with one rectangular receiver and two microphone transmitters, but if you're willing to purchase multiple $120 transmitters separately, you can record up to four tracks at once. Each transmitter includes 64GB of internal memory, which should work great as a backup. The internal memory also enables 32-bit float recording, which means the ECM-W5 can capture both quiet and loud sounds without forcing you to make gain adjustments.
Each transmitter can be attached to a separate microphone, and the transmitters themselves have 11 hours of battery life and come with magnetic backplates so you can pin them to a shirt. If you don't have a Sony camera, the receiver also includes a USB-C adapter that lets it connect to a smartphone or a PC for other recording scenarios. And while you're making adjustments on the receiver's touchscreen, you can listen to playback wirelessly using Bluetooth LE and a pair of Sony headphones.
In comparison to the $259 DJI Mic 3 or the $99 DJI Mic Mini, it's hard to imagine the ECM-W5 would be a compelling alternative unless you're specifically interested in using the new microphone kit with Sony's cameras. If you can stomach paying $400, though, 32-bit float recording could simplify your post-production workflow significantly.
The ECM-W5 is available to pre-order today for $400 and ships in November. You can also pre-order a standalone $190 ECM-W5R receiver or $120 ECM-W5T transmitter if you plan on expanding your kit.

articles.title: Android will use Gemini to warn you about scammy messages - Engadget
articles.text:
Android will use Gemini to warn you about scammy messages
Google has announced new scam and privacy protection tools for Android.
Google has announced a bunch of new, expanding and upcoming scam protections for Android users, including an opt-in setting in its Messages app that uses Gemini AI to warn you about deceptive messages. Toggling on the setting will enable Scam Detection, which taps into Google's most advanced Gemini models to evaluate the sender's intent and warn you if the messages could be coming from a bad actor. In Google's example, the sender pretended to show the recipient a photo of them with their dog. Upon being told that they had the wrong number, the sender tried to engage and asked the recipient their name.
The company explained that Android analyzes messages in Private AI Compute, which encrypts them and processes them in a secure space inaccessible to anybody else, even Google. Gemini Nano will also do on-device analysis of links in Messages to make sure they're safe before you tap on them. This will be available on Google Pixel 10+, the Samsung Galaxy S26 series, Galaxy Z Flip and Galaxy Fold 8, among other select devices. In addition, Google has redesigned its scam warnings to give you more context and extra time before tapping on links sent from numbers not in your contacts list. The new opt-in security setting is rolling out in the coming weeks.
After introducing Scam Detection in chat notifications on Pixel devices, Google is expanding its availability to more devices. The feature will warn you about potential scams right inside the message notification, so you don't even have to view it. Google has teamed up with device manufacturers, including Honor, Motorola, OPPO, OnePlus, realme, vivo and Xiaomi, which are expected to enable the feature later this year.
Meanwhile, all devices running Android 15 and newer will get automatic screen-sharing privacy later this month. The feature will hide passwords, banking information and credit card security numbers by default if you're sharing your screen that has Chrome or Android WebView open. In early December, the company is also rolling out call forwarding protection on Pixel and other select devices. The feature will block apps from secretly enabling call forwarding in the background. Android will warn you if a scammer tries to trick you into typing an MMI forwarding code — a short string of figures — to switch on call forwarding on your device.
Google has reported that it teamed up with banks in Brazil to combat bank impersonation, as well. To make sure it's actually a bank calling, Android will perform a verification check on incoming calls. If the caller fails to pass the check, Android will hang up the call and alert you. Google said Android has already blocked over three million fake calls since launching the feature in June. It's not clear if and when it will bring the safety tool stateside, but the company said it will work with more partner banks in the future.

articles.title: CEO hãng điện thoại danh tiếng tuyên bố sốc: "65 triệu để mua iPhone Duo đúng là phí tiền"
articles.text:
Face ID hoàn toàn vắng mặt trên iPhone Duo là lý do đầu tiên khiến ông cho rằng thiết bị này không đáng với mức giá gần 2.000 USD.
Dù iPhone Duo vẫn chưa chính thức mở bán, phản ứng ban đầu từ công chúng dành cho mẫu máy này nhìn chung khá tích cực kể từ khi xuất hiện tại sự kiện ra mắt gần đây của Apple.
Tuy nhiên, CEO Carl Pei của hãng công nghệ Nothing lại giữ quan điểm hoàn toàn trái ngược về chiếc điện thoại gập đầu tiên của "Táo khuyết". Theo ông, iPhone Duo chỉ là một sự lãng phí tiền bạc.
Không hề có Face ID
Apple lần đầu trình làng Face ID trên dòng iPhone X và kể từ đó đã trang bị công nghệ này cho tất cả các mẫu smartphone ra mắt sau đó. Mặc dù vậy, Face ID lại hoàn toàn vắng mặt trên iPhone Duo, và Carl Pei coi đây là lý do đầu tiên khiến ông cho rằng thiết bị này không đáng tiền. Trong video mới nhất của mình, ông nhấn mạnh rằng một thiết bị có mức giá lên tới 1.999 USD (giá bán ở Việt Nam khoảng 65 triệu) bắt buộc phải được hỗ trợ Face ID.
Dù Apple chưa đưa ra xác nhận chính thức, giới công nghệ tin rằng có hai nguyên nhân cốt lõi khiến iPhone Duo thiếu đi tính năng này.
Thứ nhất, thiết bị sở hữu độ mỏng chỉ 5,2 mm khi mở ra — một thiết kế siêu mỏng khiến việc tích hợp hệ thống cảm biến TrueDepth (vốn cần thiết để Face ID vận hành) trở nên vô cùng khó khăn về mặt vật lý. Nguyên nhân thứ hai, và có lẽ là rào cản lớn nhất, đến từ độ phức tạp trong thiết kế màn hình đôi.
Do bản chất của một chiếc điện thoại gập là có thể sử dụng ở cả trạng thái mở lẫn gập, về mặt lý thuyết Apple sẽ phải trang bị hai cụm cảm biến Face ID riêng biệt — một cho màn hình trong và một cho màn hình ngoài. Việc triển khai giải pháp này đồng nghĩa với việc phải đánh đổi độ mỏng của thiết bị.
Những đánh đổi về hệ thống camera
Bên cạnh sự thiếu vắng của Face ID, những cắt giảm ở cụm camera cũng là lý do khác khiến Carl Pei tin rằng iPhone Duo không xứng đáng với mức giá 1.999 USD.
Để dễ hình dung, mẫu máy gập này chỉ được trang bị camera trước 12 MP — một bước lùi đáng kể nếu so với camera selfie 18 MP trên chiếc iPhone 18 Pro có giá 1.199 USD. Thiết bị cũng không được trang bị cảm biến LiDAR, yếu tố vốn hỗ trợ rất đắc lực cho công việc chụp ảnh ban đêm.
Không dừng lại ở phần cứng, mảng phần mềm của máy cũng chịu sự cắt giảm. Khác với dòng iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone Duo không được cung cấp các tùy chỉnh Pro mới như điều chỉnh tốc độ màn hình trập, khẩu độ hay một số thông số chuyên sâu khác. Đáng thất vọng nhất chính là việc thiết bị gập này hoàn toàn thiếu đi một ống kính tele chuyên dụng — điểm hạn chế mà Carl Pei cũng đã chỉ ra trong video của mình.
Face ID và ống kính tele là ưu tiên hàng đầu của Apple
Apple có lẽ nhận thức rất rõ Face ID và ống kính tele chuyên dụng là hai yếu tố khiến người dùng tiếc nuối nhất trên iPhone Duo. Đó là lý do hãng được cho là đang nỗ lực tích hợp cả hai công nghệ này lên các thế hệ máy gập tiếp theo.
Theo leaker uy tín Mark Gurman, việc bổ sung hai phần cứng này hiện là ưu tiên hàng đầu cho các thế hệ iPhone Duo tương lai.
Dù vậy, khả năng chúng xuất hiện ngay trên chiếc iPhone Duo 2 là không cao. Trong bản tin của mình, Gurman nhận định phải đến thế hệ iPhone Duo thứ ba thì người dùng mới có cơ hội trải nghiệm cả ống kính tele lẫn tính năng Face ID.
Nhu cầu sở hữu Face ID vẫn rất lớn
Các bài đăng và thảo luận trên các diễn đàn công nghệ như Reddit cho thấy Face ID là một trong những tính năng cốt lõi mà người dùng cảm thấy thiếu vắng nhất trên iPhone Duo.
Một tài khoản đã đăng tải bài viết bày tỏ sự lo ngại trước việc chiếc iPhone gập thiếu đi Face ID. Một người dùng khác cũng bình luận rằng họ rất thích sự nhanh chóng, tiện lợi của Face ID trên các thiết bị Apple và thực sự sẽ cảm thấy hụt hẫng khi sử dụng thiết bị gập mà không có tính năng này.
Từ thực tế đó, cộng đồng người hâm mộ đã đưa ra một ý tưởng khá độc đáo mà Apple hoàn toàn nên cân nhắc áp dụng trên thế hệ tiếp theo: trang bị Touch ID cho màn hình ngoài và Face ID cho màn hình bên trong. Bằng cách này, hãng sẽ không còn phải bận tâm về bài toán linh kiện khi tìm cách nhồi nhét hai cảm biến Face ID vào trong một thiết bị.
iPhone Duo vẫn có nhiều điểm sáng
Sự thiếu vắng Face ID, ống kính tele cùng những cắt giảm về camera rõ ràng là những điểm trừ không nhỏ đối với một thiết bị có giá bán tiệm cận mốc 2.000 USD như iPhone Duo.
Mặc dù vậy, chúng ta cũng không thể phủ nhận những ưu điểm vượt trội mà nó mang lại. Đơn cử như chất lượng hoàn thiện thuộc hàng đỉnh cao, nếp gập gần như vô hình, hỗ trợ tần số quét ProMotion 120 Hz với tính năng Always-On, vi xử lý A20 Pro mạnh mẽ, cùng khả năng tương thích hoàn hảo với bút Apple Pencil cổng USB-C.
Gạt sang một bên những tranh cãi, Apple đã trình làng một chiếc điện thoại gập đầu tay tương đối ấn tượng, ít nhất là xét trên các thông số kỹ thuật trên giấy tờ.
Việc thiếu hụt Face ID có thể không phải yếu tố gây đáng tiếc nhất nhưng sự thiếu vắng ống kính tele có lẽ sẽ gây ra tiếc nuối, đặc biệt là khi nhìn sang các đối thủ cạnh tranh trực tiếp của iPhone Duo như Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra hay Pixel 11 Pro Fold đều đã sở hữu trang bị này.

articles.title: Masan Consumer duy trì đà tăng trưởng doanh thu hai chữ số
articles.text:
Đà tăng trưởng tiếp tục bứt phá trong quý III với doanh thu sơ bộ ước tăng 16%, khẳng định lợi thế cạnh tranh vượt trội từ hệ sinh thái thương hiệu trăm triệu USD và mạng lưới phân phối trực tiếp phủ rộng toàn quốc.
Tăng trưởng bứt phá trong bối cảnh nền kinh tế phục hồi
Theo báo cáo vĩ mô tháng 9/2026 của Kafi Research, GDP Việt Nam tăng 9,01% trong 9 tháng đầu năm, với động lực đến từ công nghiệp, xây dựng và dịch vụ. Hoạt động tiêu dùng cũng ghi nhận tín hiệu tích cực khi tổng mức bán lẻ hàng hóa và doanh thu dịch vụ tiêu dùng đạt 5.925,7 nghìn tỷ đồng, tăng 13,4% so với cùng kỳ.
Trong bối cảnh kinh tế và sức mua tiếp tục cải thiện, Masan Consumer không chỉ duy trì đà tăng trưởng mà còn ghi nhận kết quả tích cực hơn mặt bằng chung. Doanh thu sơ bộ quý III/2026 của MCH tăng khoảng 16% so với cùng kỳ, trong khi lợi nhuận từ hoạt động kinh doanh (EBIT) đạt mức tăng trưởng hai chữ số.
Vượt tốc độ tăng trưởng chung của ngành hàng tiêu dùng nhanh
Bên cạnh GDP, tốc độ tăng trưởng của thị trường hàng tiêu dùng nhanh (FMCG) là cơ sở so sánh sát thực hơn với hoạt động kinh doanh của Masan Consumer.
Theo báo cáo phân tích tháng 9/2026 của TCBS Research, doanh thu MCH tăng 13,6% trong nửa đầu năm 2026, trong khi thị trường FMCG Việt Nam tăng khoảng 4 - 5%.
Thị trường hàng tiêu dùng nhanh Việt Nam đang dần phục hồi sau giai đoạn tăng trưởng chậm. Theo dữ liệu TCBS tổng hợp, tăng trưởng ngành cải thiện từ mức 1,5% trong quý II/2025 lên 4,5% trong quý I và 4,8% trong quý II/2026. TCBS nhận định, kết quả kinh doanh của Masan Consumer trong giai đoạn này cho thấy doanh nghiệp đang mở rộng thị phần, thay vì chỉ hưởng lợi từ sự phục hồi chung của thị trường.
Nhìn dài hạn, từ năm 2017 đến 12 tháng gần nhất kết thúc vào tháng 6/2026, doanh thu và lợi nhuận từ hoạt động kinh doanh (EBIT) của Masan Consumer tăng bình quân lần lượt 11% và 15% mỗi năm. Kết quả này cho thấy tăng trưởng của doanh nghiệp không chỉ là diễn biến ngắn hạn, mà đã được duy trì qua nhiều năm.
Những kết quả này cho thấy tốc độ tăng trưởng của Masan Consumer không chỉ nổi bật trong thời gian gần đây mà còn được duy trì trong nhiều năm qua.
Thương hiệu và mạng lưới phân phối tạo nền tảng tăng trưởng
Theo TCBS Research, Masan Consumer sở hữu 5 thương hiệu đạt doanh thu trên 100 triệu USD mỗi năm, gồm Chin-Su, Nam Ngư, Omachi, Kokomi và Wake-Up 247. Nhóm thương hiệu này đóng góp khoảng 70% doanh thu và 80% lợi nhuận gộp của doanh nghiệp.
Sức mạnh thương hiệu giúp MCH tiếp tục phát triển sản phẩm trên những ngành hàng đã có vị thế. Chin-Su mở rộng từ nước mắm, tương ớt sang các loại xốt và gia vị tiện lợi; Omachi phát triển thêm những lựa chọn bữa ăn cao cấp, trong khi Nam Ngư bổ sung các dòng sản phẩm đáp ứng nhiều nhu cầu chế biến khác nhau.
Bên cạnh thương hiệu, mạng lưới phân phối giúp doanh nghiệp đưa sản phẩm đến người tiêu dùng trên quy mô lớn. Theo TCBS, Masan Consumer có hệ thống phân phối trực tiếp tới khoảng 450.000 điểm bán trên cả nước.
Thông qua nền tảng Retail Supreme, doanh nghiệp đang tăng số lượng sản phẩm và ngành hàng được bán tại các cửa hàng hiện hữu. Thay vì chỉ mở rộng số điểm bán, MCH có thể tăng doanh thu bằng cách phục vụ nhiều nhu cầu hơn tại mỗi cửa hàng.
Ngoài các ngành hàng chủ lực, những lĩnh vực mới cũng đang đóng góp vào tăng trưởng. Trong 8 tháng đầu năm 2026, doanh thu ngành hàng chăm sóc cá nhân và gia đình tăng 25,6% so với cùng kỳ, trong khi kinh doanh quốc tế tăng 19,1%.
Nhờ đó, tăng trưởng của Masan Consumer được hỗ trợ bởi nhiều nguồn: các thương hiệu chủ lực tiếp tục phát triển, mạng lưới phân phối được khai thác hiệu quả hơn và những ngành hàng, thị trường mới bổ sung doanh thu.
Một điểm đáng chú ý khác là tăng trưởng doanh thu đi cùng khả năng sinh lời. Năm 2025, Masan Consumer ghi nhận biên lợi nhuận gộp 45,5% và lợi nhuận sau thuế 6.764 tỷ đồng. Theo TCBS, sức mạnh thương hiệu cùng mô hình kinh doanh sử dụng vốn hiệu quả là những yếu tố hỗ trợ khả năng sinh lời của doanh nghiệp.
Kết quả kinh doanh nhiều năm qua và diễn biến mới nhất cho thấy Masan Consumer đang duy trì tốc độ mở rộng hoạt động cao hơn mức tăng chung, đồng thời vượt tốc độ tăng trưởng của thị trường hàng tiêu dùng nhanh trong giai đoạn được so sánh.
Trong bối cảnh kinh tế Việt Nam duy trì đà tăng trưởng tích cực, kết quả kinh doanh của Masan Consumer cho thấy doanh nghiệp không chỉ hưởng lợi từ sức mua chung mà còn tạo ra tăng trưởng từ chính năng lực cạnh tranh của mình. Sức mạnh thương hiệu, hiệu quả phân phối và việc mở rộng ngành hàng là những yếu tố góp phần tạo nên sự khác biệt về tốc độ tăng trưởng của MCH so với thị trường.
(Nguồn: Masan Consumer)

articles.title: Electric vehicle sales in the US are showing signs of life | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Don’t go writing the obituary for the U.S. electric vehicle just yet. After sales tanked following the cancellation of tax credits last year, they’ve been growing for the last three consecutive quarters, according to a new report from Cox Automotive.
EVs captured 6.1% of the U.S. market, their best showing since the third quarter of 2025. The data shows that the EV market is “finding its footing again,” Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of industry insights at Cox Automotive, said in an analysis that accompanied the new report. EV prices have become more competitive, and high gas prices have sparked renewed consumer interest, she added.
Toyota, Rivian, and Subaru led the pack. Sales of the Toyota bZ and Lexus RZ about doubled following a refresh that hit dealerships late last year. The updated models adopted Tesla-style charging ports and received larger batteries, more powerful motors, and faster charging times.
Meanwhile, Tesla’s sales dropped by 20% year-over-year. Tesla still retains the first-mover advantage, though, selling over half of all EVs during the third quarter.
The recovery in the U.S. mimics what occurred in Germany after the government stopped incentives for EV purchases in November 2023, a year earlier than expected. The following month, sales fell by more than half. But after hitting that low, the market steadily recovered. German EV sales in August, the most recent month for which data is available, were the second highest on record.

articles.title: LG adds DTS:X and Google Cast to its Sound Suite home theater system - Engadget
articles.text:
LG adds DTS:X and Google Cast to its Sound Suite home theater system
The company also teased a 'Media Connect Hub' for DTS:X devices that's currently in development.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
LG is known for its soundbars and surround sound systems as much as it is for its OLED TVs, and one of its more interesting products in that realm is Sound Suite. That premium system lets you pick and choose select speakers à la carte to best fit your space, place them where you want and then use Dolby Atmos FlexConnect tech make them perform well — a nice setup, if you can afford it.
Now, LG is adding some new features to Sound Suite in response to customer feedback. It now supports DTS:X for new surround sound options, along with Google Cast, dual W7 subwoofers and more flexible Wi-Fi configurations. LG also teased a new "Media Connect Hub" for DTS:X devices that's currently in development.
The key new feature is DTS:X support for the H7 soundbar, the centerpiece of LG's Sound Suite. That feature, it said, will give "home theater enthusiasts additional ways to enjoy immersive, multi-dimensional audio from compatible content and source devices." Another big update is Google Cast support on the H7 soundbar so that you can stream content like music and podcasts directly to LG Sound Suite systems.
In keeping with its flexible multi-speaker underpinning, Sound Suite is also expanding compatibility in home networked environments with support for Wi-Fi 6 GHz networks and 5 GHz DFS channels. That, LG said, will give users more stereo and multi-speaker configuration options within the Sound Suite environment. Finally, LG is adding support for dual W7 subwoofer setups, for those who want to max out on low end sound.
As for the Media Connect Hub, LG said it will enable DTS:X "from compatible external source devices and further expand access to DTS:X content." That's quite vague, but it could be a way to connect Blu-ray or 4K Ultra HD disc players to the Sound Suite environment, along with other devices that support DTS:X. That's just a guess, though, and we'll need to wait for more news from LG on the subject. The new software updates are already rolling out in some regions, but timing and availability could be different depending on your location.

articles.title: Phát hiện cảnh tượng lạ tại một trung tâm thương mại: Nhìn kỹ 5 lần mới hiểu chuyện gì đang xảy ra
articles.text:
Những người chứng kiến mô tả hai "cha con" thong thả bước đi khắp nơi.
Một người đàn ông ở Thành Đô, Trung Quốc gần đây đã gây chú ý khi bị bắt gặp đang dắt tay một con robot hình người cỡ nhỏ đi dạo qua trung tâm thương mại, chăm sóc cỗ máy như một người cha đang dẫn con nhỏ đi chơi.
Cảnh tượng này diễn ra tại MixC Thành Đô, một trung tâm thương mại lớn ở thành phố phía tây nam Trung Quốc. Những người chứng kiến mô tả hai "cha con" thong thả bước đi khắp khu phức hợp, người đàn ông nắm tay robot di chuyển với nhịp độ thư thái như thể đây là điều tự nhiên nhất trên đời.
Robot hình người đã trở thành hình ảnh ngày càng quen thuộc tại các đô thị Trung Quốc trong năm qua, phần lớn xuất hiện dưới dạng sản phẩm thử nghiệm của các công ty công nghệ hoặc chiêu trò thu hút khách của trung tâm thương mại. Điều khiến đoạn clip này lan truyền rộng rãi chính là sự bình dị, đời thường của nó - không phải một buổi ra mắt sản phẩm thương mại, mà chỉ đơn giản là một người đàn ông cùng cỗ máy của mình đi dạo dạo quanh vào ngày Chủ nhật.
Đoạn video không cho biết đơn vị sản xuất ra con robot hay liệu đây có phải là một phương thức truyền thông đã được lên kế hoạch trước hay không.
Robot hình người giá rẻ đang trở thành tâm điểm chú ý tại Trung Quốc khi các nhà sản xuất nỗ lực đưa công nghệ này từ các nhà xưởng, phòng thí nghiệm vào hộ gia đình, trường học và doanh nghiệp nhỏ.
Bước ngoặt lớn nằm ở chi phí: cảm biến, pin, động cơ rẻ hơn cùng năng lực sản xuất hàng loạt đang giúp các robot hình người cơ bản trở nên dễ tiếp cận hơn nhiều so với các mẫu thử nghiệm đắt đỏ có giá lên tới hàng chục nghìn USD trước đây.
Dù mức giá đã hạ nhiệt, tính ứng dụng thực tế vẫn phụ thuộc vào thời lượng pin, độ an toàn, khả năng di chuyển ổn định, chất lượng phần mềm, điều khiển bằng giọng nói và liệu robot có thể xử lý tốt các công việc nhà thực tế hay không.
Câu chuyện lớn hơn ở đây là ngành robot có thể đang bước vào giai đoạn tương tự như smartphone trước đây - thời điểm mà mức giá giảm mạnh có thể nhanh chóng biến công nghệ tưởng chừng như đến từ tương lai này thành các sản phẩm tiêu dùng phổ biến hàng ngày.
Nguồn: CNN

articles.title: TimeTeller puts our internal clocks at the center of personalized medicine | TechCrunch
articles.text:
At-home health testing has been mired in overblown claims and outright fraud. But German startup TimeTeller, which has developed a saliva test kit to help anyone understand their circadian rhythm, is led by CEO Angela Relógio, who is the polar opposite of Theranos’ disgraced founder Elizabeth Holmes.
Relógio is a physicist-engineer and molecular biologist who spent years researching oncology, circadian biology, and systems medicine in Germany before leaving academia to build TimeTeller. She is careful about what the test can and can’t do today.
It would be easy to oversell: Relógio’s last name means “clock” in her native Portuguese, and TimeTeller has the potential to reduce side effects from cancer treatment and improve outcomes by timing treatment to each patient’s internal clock. That’s also why she’s careful to warn that TimeTeller itself operates on two timelines.
The long-term goal is to determine when cancer treatments will be better tolerated and most effective, and doing so much more granularly than just telling whether someone is a morning person or a night owl. But its direct-to-consumer kit won’t help patients figure that out on their own. “That is something that we need to calculate for every single medicine; we do that in the context of clinical studies,” Relógio cautioned.
According to Relógio, TimeTeller started accepting direct orders because of demand from longevity clinics, which focus on healthy aging and understand that individual data on a person’s circadian rhythm can be used to offer personalized advice on sleep, nutrition, light exposure, and physical activity.
TimeTeller could also apply to metabolic diseases (such as diabetes) and neurodegenerative diseases (such as Alzheimer’s), performance, and women’s health, but cancer is its core mission. It was while studying cancer that Relógio made the discovery that led her to leave academia.
She noticed that many cancer patients stopped or started their treatment because of side effects. “As a scientist, that was just impossible to watch, particularly when I was convinced that part of the problem might not only be what treatment we give, but when we give it,” Relógio said. This led her to develop the circadian rhythm test at the core of TimeTeller — which she knew had to become a company.
“I personally funded our first patent because I strongly believed that this discovery should not remain in scientific publications,” she said. The startup spun out of Berlin’s Charité university hospital but has since moved to Medical School Hamburg, which provided access to patients and funding. It also offered a fallback: backup employment for TimeTeller’s team of 10 if the company couldn’t pay them.
That’s a safety net TimeTeller may not need. Having enlisted biochemist and market access specialist Benjamin Dose as a co-founder, the startup secured a partnership with Techniker Krankenkasse, one of Germany’s largest health insurance providers. The partnership started out as a reimbursement deal in which the insurer pays back the cost of the test for a subset of cancer patients, and both sides are now ready to expand it to more of the insurer’s 12 million members, Relógio said.
Despite her caveats about the direct-to-consumer test, TimeTeller has become a solution that cancer patients can actually access. Ahead of her appearance at TechCrunch Disrupt, where Relógio appeared onstage today in San Francisco as part of our storied Startup Battlefield competition, she made clear that the company has broader ambitions: a future in which asking “when” is central to precision medicine, because “almost every process in our body is timed.”
You aren’t too late to join the action at Disrupt. Come for the headliners; stay to see who wins this year’s no-strings check from TechCrunch — and the attention of the hundreds of VCs in attendance.

articles.title: Ăn Cùng Bà Tuyết lên tiếng về hàng mang nhãn hiệu bị tiêu hủy tại Nhật Bản
articles.text:
Công ty Cổ phần Thực phẩm Ăn Cùng Bà Tuyết vừa phát đi thông báo chính thức liên quan đến thông tin sản phẩm mang nhãn hiệu này bị cơ quan kiểm dịch Nhật Bản tiêu hủy tại tỉnh Ibaraki.
Theo doanh nghiệp, ngày 9/10/2026, Bộ Nông Lâm Thủy sản Nhật Bản (MAFF) công bố thông tin về việc kiểm tra, xử lý các sản phẩm thuộc diện kiểm dịch động vật tại một cửa hàng ở thành phố Koga, tỉnh Ibaraki. Trong số các sản phẩm bị xử lý có hàng hóa mang nhãn hiệu “Ăn Cùng Bà Tuyết”.
Trong thông báo, Ăn Cùng Bà Tuyết khẳng định tôn trọng và nghiêm túc chấp hành quy định pháp luật tại Nhật Bản cũng như các quốc gia, vùng lãnh thổ nơi sản phẩm có thể được tiêu thụ.
Doanh nghiệp cho biết hiện chưa xuất khẩu sản phẩm sang Nhật Bản. Công ty cũng chưa chỉ định hoặc ủy quyền cho bất kỳ tổ chức, cá nhân nào thực hiện hoạt động xuất khẩu, nhập khẩu hoặc phân phối sản phẩm tại thị trường này.
Doanh nghiệp khuyến nghị khách hàng, đối tác không tự ý mang theo, gửi, vận chuyển hoặc kinh doanh sản phẩm thuộc diện kiểm dịch tại Nhật Bản khi chưa đáp ứng đầy đủ các điều kiện pháp luật.
Công ty cho biết sẽ rà soát hệ thống đại lý, nhà phân phối và gian hàng thương mại điện tử. Doanh nghiệp sẽ yêu cầu các đơn vị không nhận đơn, quảng cáo hoặc hỗ trợ gửi sản phẩm Ăn Cùng Bà Tuyết sang những thị trường mà công ty chưa xuất khẩu chính ngạch, trong đó có Nhật Bản.
Dẫn thông tin từ MAFF, doanh nghiệp cho biết đơn vị kiểm tra và tiêu hủy hàng hóa là Trạm Kiểm dịch Động vật thuộc cơ quan này. Cửa hàng bị xử lý do đưa hàng hóa vào Nhật Bản qua đường bưu chính quốc tế và bày bán khi chưa có giấy chứng nhận kiểm dịch. Lô hàng bị tiêu hủy gồm các sản phẩm từ thịt của nhiều nhãn hàng có xuất xứ Việt Nam và Indonesia.
Nhật Bản nghiêm cấm nhập khẩu các sản phẩm từ thịt không có giấy chứng nhận kiểm dịch do cơ quan có thẩm quyền của nước xuất khẩu cấp. Quy định này nhằm phòng ngừa dịch bệnh trên vật nuôi và áp dụng chung đối với các sản phẩm thuộc diện kiểm dịch, không phân biệt thương hiệu hay quốc gia xuất xứ.

articles.title: Startup Việt bất ngờ nhận 'khoản vốn' 200 triệu đồng từ ông lớn AI Anthropic mà không mất 1% cổ phần nào
articles.text:
Thay vì bỏ ra hàng trăm triệu đồng chi phí hạ tầng và phần mềm mỗi năm, nhiều startup Việt đang âm thầm tận dụng gói tài trợ khủng từ Anthropic, biến AI từ một khoản chi phí đắt đỏ thành "trợ lý miễn phí" 100%.
Trong bối cảnh chi phí vận hành ngày càng đắt đỏ, việc tối ưu hóa ngân sách luôn là bài toán đau đầu với các startup và những người làm sáng tạo nội dung độc lập. Mới đây, bài chia sẻ của anh Nguyễn Xuân Sơn một người hoạt động trong lĩnh vực công nghệ và truyền thông đã thu hút sự chú ý lớn từ cộng đồng khi anh tiết lộ vừa đăng ký thành công chương trình Claude Startups của Anthropic.
"Đăng ký thử, ai ngờ tiết kiệm được hơn 200 triệu thật", anh Sơn hồ hởi chia sẻ trên facebook cá nhân sau khi nhận được email xác nhận tài trợ chính thức.
Theo thông tin được chia sẻ, ngay sau khi hồ sơ đăng ký được xét duyệt thành công, dự án của anh Sơn đã chính thức nhận được trọn gói quyền lợi cao cấp từ Anthropic. Đứng đầu trong danh mục tài trợ này là 1 năm sử dụng hoàn toàn miễn phí gói Claude Team - giải pháp tối ưu giúp hỗ trợ tối đa cho làm việc nhóm, quản lý dự án và xử lý các tác vụ AI có khối lượng dữ liệu lớn.
Bên cạnh tài khoản làm việc nhóm, gói hỗ trợ còn đính kèm 1.000 USD API credit. Đây là khoản ngân sách đắt giá cho phép các nhà phát triển kết nối trực tiếp mô hình AI Claude vào các hệ thống tự động hóa và ứng dụng riêng của doanh nghiệp.
Tính tổng giá trị quy đổi trên thị trường hiện tại, chương trình hỗ trợ này đã giúp chủ dự án cắt giảm được hơn 200 triệu đồng chi phí phần mềm và hạ tầng AI chỉ trong vòng 12 tháng vận hành.
Một trong những ứng dụng thực tế đầu tiên được anh Sơn thử nghiệm ngay là thiết kế thumbnail cho các bài đăng và video. Theo anh Sơn chia sẻ, thông thường việc thuê ngoài thiết kế các mẫu thumbnail chất lượng cao có thể tốn từ vài trăm nghìn đồng cho mỗi bức ảnh, chưa kể thời gian chỉnh sửa qua lại. Nhờ áp dụng quy trình làm việc với Claude, từ khâu lên ý tưởng, phác thảo bố cục cho đến hoàn thiện sản phẩm đều được thực hiện tự động hóa.
Dành cho những ai chưa biết, Claude Startups là chương trình tài trợ do Anthropic triển khai nhằm hỗ trợ các công ty khởi nghiệp và các dự án tiềm năng trên toàn cầu.
Chương trình này hướng tới việc cung cấp tài nguyên tính toán, quyền truy cập sớm vào các mô hình AI cao cấp nhất (như Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3 Opus) cùng ngân sách API credit để các team dễ dàng thử nghiệm, phát triển sản phẩm và tối ưu hóa quy trình vận hành.
Tuy nhiên chương trình này đã bị tạm dừng do lượng đăng ký quá cao trên phạm vi toàn cầu.

articles.title: Ambrosia Energy will build a 10 GWh factory in Texas to make batteries for off-grid data centers | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Ambrosia Energy has begun work on a massive, 10 gigawatt-hour battery factory near Austin, Texas, co-founder and CEO Ben Longmier announced onstage Tuesday at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco.
“That allows us to build about a 300 megawatt power plant per year out at our field sites,” he said.
The factory will occupy 150,000 square feet, and Longmier said that Ambrosia plans to reach full production in two to three years.
The startup emerged from stealth in June to build power plants for data centers at a cost of $100 per megawatt hour. Longmier and his co-founder, Sara Spangelo, had settled on solar plus batteries as the cheapest option that’s the fastest to deploy. Solar panels power the load during the day and charge the batteries, which discharge at night and on cloudy days to keep the data center operating round the clock.
Longmier and Spangelo previously founded the satellite constellation startup Swarm, which they sold to SpaceX.
Ambrosia is also beginning work on its first commercial power plant in West Texas later this year, Longmier said. The facility will pair 300 megawatts of solar panels with 660 megawatt-hours of batteries to deliver 30 megawatts of continuous power, with a goal of 99.3% uptime.
Even with “overbuilding” solar and batteries to deliver continuous uptime, Longmier said the company can be profitable at $100 per megawatt-hour, making it competitive with natural gas turbines that many hyperscalers are planning to use to power their data centers.
Sections of Ambrosia’s first pilot-scale power plant have been operating continuously for more than 100 days, Longmier said. The pilot is capable of generating 200 kilowatts of electricity 24/7.
To hit its cost targets, Ambrosia has been finding ways to simplify its components, including solar mounts and battery packs. By reducing part counts, and manufacturing many components in a factory, the startup has been able to reduce costs relative to buying from outside suppliers.
“We buy existing cells and we make our own pack in-house, and it has the fewest parts by a factor of about 100 compared to any other competitor we’ve seen,” Longmier said. ”We’ve been able to get to about 1.3x the cost of the bare cell compared to about a 5- or 7x for most stationary storage systems.”

Theo kỳ hạn, các giao dịch VND chủ yếu tập trung vào kỳ hạn qua đêm (96% tổng doanh số giao dịch VND), kỳ hạn 1 tuần (2% tổng doanh số giao dịch VND).
Giao dịch USD tập trung chủ yếu ở kỳ hạn qua đêm và 1 tuần, chiếm lần lượt 75% và 21%.

articles.title: WhatsApp adds a guest option for joining calls without an account - Engadget
articles.text:
WhatsApp adds a guest option for joining calls without an account
It’s also working on calendar integrations for later this year.
WhatsApp is adding more flexibility for talking to people who aren't regular users of its service. The Meta-owned company has announced the addition of a feature dubbed guest calling. With this option, somebody can join a call even if they don't have a WhatsApp account.
The guest calling support mirrors the little-known option to join a FaceTime call without an Apple account or device. Like that feature, there are some restrictions for participating in a WhatsApp call via the guest method. Guests cannot start a call; they can only receive and accept invitations. They'll also have to be approved by the call host before they can join. A guest will not be able to view other users' phone numbers, send messages or add more members to the call. However, they will be able to join either 1:1 or group calls from a browser, and once approved, guests will be able to use core tools such as screen sharing, raising their hand, and reacting with the thumbs up and heart emojis. Guests also won't have any time limits placed on their participation in a call.
The company noted that it plans to further facilitate collaboration with the future rollout of a plugin for calendar integrations. Once launched "later this year," the plugin will allow WhatApp calls can be created from Google or Outlook calendars.
WhatsApp has kept a brisk pace with feature updates this year, many of them aimed at making the service more accessible, secure and appealing for business users. The addition of usernames allowed people to keep their phone numbers private, while more incremental adds from 2026 include encrypted web calls and account signups via iPad. The service may also offer a much-requested option to schedule messages in advance.

articles.title: McKinsey is making job applicants spar with a fake AI client
articles.text:
Consulting firm McKinsey & Company is going to ask some entry-level candidates to have a 10-minute conversation with an AI simulation of a client as part of the interview process, according to The Wall Street Journal.
McKinsey is making job applicants spar with a fake AI client
Some entry-level McKinsey candidates will have a 10-minute conversation with a simulated client as part of the interview process.
The AI simulation “aims to reflect 80% of the scenarios McKinsey consultants might encounter in their day-to-day work,” the WSJ says, and it isn’t designed to “mimic an unhinged client.” The AI won’t score the candidates — humans will be in the room to assess the candidates and see how well they deal with the simulated situations.
The McKinsey tool will be in testing for undergrads seeking business-analyst jobs in “some” offices in North America this fall, and the WSJ says “hundreds” may use it.
Other companies are also building tools to use AI avatars as part of the job interview process, and my colleague Hayden Field tried some of them out for a video we published in March.

articles.title: OpenAI hands its data centre and compute operation to a former xAI executive
articles.text:
OpenAI has put its compute and infrastructure businesses under Uday Ruddarraju, who ran infrastructure at Elon Musk’s xAI until July 2025. Sachin Katti, who had been overseeing infrastructure and led the $30B Georgia build, leaves the role within weeks and stays on as an adviser.
OpenAI has put compute and infrastructure under one executive. Uday Ruddarraju, who ran infrastructure at Elon Musk’s xAI, takes both. Sachin Katti, who had been overseeing infrastructure, leaves within weeks.
Bloomberg reported the change on Wednesday. Katti plans to stay on as an adviser, and the business leaders under him keep their jobs.
Ruddarraju joined OpenAI in July 2025 and became chief technology officer for compute this July. At xAI he worked on the Grok 3 training run across 100,000 GPUs.
“Sachin has done an incredible job maintaining the commercial partnerships,” he told Bloomberg. He expects a smooth handover, and said he must now spend more time on the commercial side.
The appointment names someone OpenAI would not name in August. When it confirmed that its data centre chief had left, it had already hired a compute CTO but would not say who. It was Ruddarraju.
Chris Malone was not the only exit. Peter Hoeschele, central to Stargate, left for Meta earlier this year with two colleagues. Data Center Dynamics names Keith Heyde and Shamez Hemani.
Katti arrived from Intel late last year, where he was chief technology and AI officer, and the same outlet dates his Stargate takeover to March. He oversaw the $30B Georgia site, the first OpenAI designed and led itself.
He also oversaw an 8-gigawatt project in Ohio with SB Energy and Nvidia. Nvidia has guaranteed up to $105B in lease and power payments there, Axios reported from a securities filing.
Katti had also run GPT-Infra since July, which uses OpenAI models for work such as designing semiconductors. That effort moves to Richard Ho, the company’s chip chief, who said this month he does not fully trust the models’ design changes.
“I’m proud of what we’ve built and have total confidence in Uday and the team,” Katti said. He is looking forward to building something new.
What Ruddarraju inherits is almost entirely American. OpenAI paused Stargate UK in April, citing British electricity prices more than four times US levels and unresolved copyright rules.
The UK government called the decision disappointing. The Guardian later reported that OpenAI had never visited the north-east England site it announced.
OpenAI’s one announced European site is a 230-megawatt data centre in Norway, revealed in July 2025. Ohio alone is about 35 times larger. Most of the $856B compute bill shown to investors will be spent across the Atlantic.

articles.title: Hiyd is a health tracker that attaches to the watch you already wear | TechCrunch
articles.text:
If you’re a watch enthusiast, you probably don’t want to exchange your prized timepiece for a bulky fitness tracker. But Hiyd founder Salah Batroukh doesn’t think people should have to sacrifice fashion for function.
“We don’t think that health tracking needs to be this overly conscious decision where you have to change something about the way you look,” Batroukh told TechCrunch. “That’s the ethos of the entire company. Our plan is to build out this product ecosystem of invisible health tracking.”
Hiyd’s first device to make health tracking look cooler is a small, slim disc that attaches to the back of your watch via microsuction, a material technology that allows the sensor to sit flush under your watch without magnets or adhesive. That way, it won’t leave any residue or mess with the mechanics of watches that keep time using magnets.
“Microsuction is essentially a textured silicone, with hundreds of tiny pockets per square inch molded into a pliable sheet. So when you press on it, it pushes air out of all those pockets, and you end up with a vacuum — just like traditional suction cups but scaled down incredibly,” Batroukh explained. “It works incredibly at stopping shear forces, but a little bit of prying allows it to pop right off, which is ideal for us. It’s also incredibly thin at just 0.3 mm with our manufacturing processes.”
According to Batroukh, the sensor, which measures 2.7 mm thick and weighs 7 grams, collects biometrics similar to those of leading wearables, including heart rate, heart rate variability, sleep staging, movement, calories burned, and VO2 max estimations, then syncs to an iOS or Android app. In order to fine-tune the sensor, Hiyd’s team is filming themselves doing various activities, then labeling those datasets to train its AI.
“We go for a walk and say, ‘This is somebody walking, this is somebody jogging, this is somebody running,’” he said. “The one thing that AI is really good at is data analysis, so we can basically fit a lot of heuristic analysis into our sets really quickly.”
On its app, Hiyd is also working to incorporate nutrition tracking. The goal isn’t to count calories, but rather to help users glean insights about how their eating habits impact their sleep quality or workout performance.
“What we will do is say like, ‘Hey, on days where you work out at 10 p.m. instead of 10 a.m., your sleep quality is actually worse,’ and that’ll be specific to you,” he said. “Or it’ll say, ‘Hey, we think you had a less deep sleep last night because you had a slice of cake before you went to bed, and the sugar affected it.’”
Batroukh spent about seven years as a manufacturing design engineer at Apple, a company synonymous with iconic hardware. But he wanted to know if he could design something great without the support of a global brand and a multitrillion-dollar market cap.
“One of the reasons I left Apple was a lot of the products became a little bit more about being an Apple product, rather than being something for the customer,” he said. “[Hiyd] gives me the opportunity to do the exact opposite.”
Batroukh is joined by fellow founders Omar Shakir, an experienced mechanical engineer who is the startup’s CTO, and Mahamad Charawi, who is its head of software. (Charawi previously co-led the Y Combinator-backed startup Laudspeaker through its sale.)
Hiyd is bringing its tiny sensor to the big stage at TechCrunch Disrupt, where the company is competing as one of the top 20 companies at Startup Battlefield on Wednesday. (Don’t miss out on the action.) In November, the company plans to launch a Kickstarter. So far, over 16,000 people have made deposits to secure Hiyd’s first units.

articles.title: CMF's first portable speakers are shaped like milk cartons and pair together - Engadget
articles.text:
CMF's first portable speakers are shaped like milk cartons and pair together
They look like something from Teenage Engineering or IKEA.
Surprisingly, CMF (nor its sister brand Nothing) has only now tried its hand at portable speakers. Naturally, it had to do it differently and the result is two different speaker options, both shaped like cute, vivid milk cartons.
Available now, the CMF Speaker S ($59) and Speaker M ($109) look great, with a few features and specs I'm surprised to see at this price point. Both speakers come in orange, turquoise and white, and the control knob come in different shapes and colors too; I told you: cute. You can even swap out the cover plate and knob between devices. The knob controls volume but can also skip tracks and rewind. I like the hole in the top corner of the speakers, which makes it easy to attach to a bag or tent.
The smaller Speaker S has a 45mm full-range driver, and a pair of passive radiators boost bassier tones. Meanwhile, the Speaker M has a 10W tweeter, dual drivers and even a 25W woofer, with two speaker outlets, and is roughly double the height of the Speaker S. Both speakers have Bluetooth 6.0 connectivity, IP68 dust and water resistance ratings and CMF claims both can play music for up to 18 hours. They have USB-C ports for charging, but this can also be used as audio input. The new speakers also support NFC pairing, Google Fast Pair and even Microsoft Swift Pair.
At this price, I was most surprised to see the option to pair two Speaker S or Speaker M together. Oddly, you can't combine an S and an M. They also support Auracast, which is appearing in increasingly more devices from more companies. I received a pair of the smaller speakers and they're surprisingly rich-sounding, given the size (and price). One warning: there's no USB-C cable included, but I'm sure many of us have a spare.
Like some past Teenage Engineering products, CMF says it will release the design files so devoted listeners can 3D print custom handles and accessories. Both speakers are available now on Nothing's retail site.

articles.title: The best feature of Apple’s HomeView might be its simplicity
articles.text:
I’m just going to come right out and say it. I love the approach Apple has taken with the HomeView. I think it’s the shared, always-available household interface that my family might finally use. Is Apple’s first smart display my dream smart home dashboard? No. But is it the right product for Apple Home at this moment? Absolutely.
The best feature of Apple’s HomeView might be its simplicity
If Apple’s first smart display finally gets my family to actually use my smart home, I’ll consider it a win.
A lot of initial reactions to the $299 HomeView (which looks like a giant Apple Watch on a flatter metallic HomePod Mini) ask why you would want it when you can do most of what it offers on your iPhone or iPad. And yes, its features replicate many of the things you already do on the devices you use all the time. But that’s kind of the point. HomeView gives you another interface for those things, but crucially one that is always powered, always unlocked, and always in the same spot in your home, making it easy to walk up to and interact with.
I’ve tried using an iPad to control my smart home, run my family’s calendar, and be a shared device for controlling music. It wasn’t great. I’ll have to test HomeView, of course, but my initial impression is that this could be a much better solution for those use cases.
Most iPads are more expensive, have worse speakers, and do not like to be plugged in all the time (I present my sad, warped iPad Mini as tribute). An iPad can’t be a hub for your Apple Home; HomeView can. An iPad famously isn’t a good multiuser device, and controlling home devices on one requires it staying logged in to your personal iCloud account; HomeView offers Apple’s first crack at easy multiuser switching.
Apple designed HomeView as a communal device that sits in a fixed place in the home. This means it’s always where you expect it to be, which matters when you want to adjust the thermostat or can’t find your phone and want to check your calendar. Not having a battery or detachable screen is a feature for me, because devices that do inevitably wander off and die under a couch cushion.
And while many people are fine using their personal phones and tablets to interact with the digital world when at home, and don’t want yet another device with a screen on their countertop or wall, the millions of Echo Shows, Google Nest Hubs, Skylight Calendars, and the like in homes today are a good indicator that there’s interest in this type of interface.
As Apple’s uncharacteristically chaotic launch video shows, HomeView targets a new demographic for the company: busy, Apple-centric households. One feature I’m most interested in is HomeView’s role as a home video phone. Do you know how many times I’ve tried to call my daughter when I’m not home, and her phone is dead or on silent? Based on Apple’s video, if she’s home, my call can now ring on the HomeView. I’ve occasionally used the drop-in feature on Echo smart speakers to get her attention, further proof of the advantage of always-on home devices.
I see HomeView as filling the awkward space where families don’t want phones at the dinner table or on the kitchen counter, but still want to check what time Zoey’s soccer game is or look up the origin of French toast (yeah, just kidding). This inevitably ends with one person pulling out their phone, which gives everyone else implicit permission to do the same.
Smart displays and speakers from Amazon and Google already help with this to some extent, but Apple’s version comes without ads (see the Echo Show) and may have a longer lifespan (RIP Pixel Tablet). Siri AI’s much-hyped “personal context” capabilities, in which it can scan your text messages and emails and serve up relevant information to up to six members of your household, also give it an edge here.
I asked Kaiann Drance, vice president of product marketing for home at Apple, why Apple chose now for its biggest smart home push yet. She said Siri AI and the personal context it brings, which she called Apple’s “privacy story,” came together with a device designed specifically for the home. “With the magic of Siri AI, it comes together in a way that we haven’t been able to deliver before,” she said.
As the Siri AI capabilities continue to evolve, the home experience is fitting to be able to interact with in a natural way.”
— Lilian Rincon, Apple
Siri AI made this possible because it’s “much more capable,” said Lilian Rincon, vice president of product marketing for AI at Apple. She also pointed to its new conversational abilities. “It’s great because you can just ask it to change the temperature on your thermostat in a very natural way. As the Siri AI capabilities continue to evolve, the home experience is fitting to be able to interact with in this natural way.” On why now, Rincon says the natural-language shift is the point where AI goes mainstream. “Because now it can be … my mother-in-law or the Gen Z who’s in college, both of them can use this in the way that they naturally speak and get what they want.”
Siri AI in the home has another big advantage over the competition: It doesn’t say too much. Based on the demos I saw, and my time using Siri AI on the iPhone, when you ask it to do something, it does it without peppering you with follow-up questions. Rincon confirmed this is by design. “A lot of these assistants out there are always asking questions because they want more information,” she said. “For us, it isn’t about that. We’re there to get it done, take an action for you, show you what you need to get done, and then really get out of the way.”
My first reaction to hearing about HomeView’s smart home features, which are basically just what the Apple Home app on your phone can do, was disappointment. I had hoped that, along with new hardware, Apple would bring more functionality and deeper Apple Intelligence integration to Apple Home to make the smart home smarter. I’m still waiting on that.
On reflection, I’m okay with this — for now. Apple trying to make the smart home easier for everyone to use can only be a good thing. As always, the smart home’s most important goal is to come up with an easier way to turn on the lights.
Apple trying to make the smart home easier for everyone to use can only be a good thing.
HomeView’s simplicity may put off hardcore home automation enthusiasts, but I’d argue it’s perfect for their long-suffering spouses. I’ve tried every version of physical smart home control interface in my home, and you know who hasn’t used any of them? My family.
Because my family all have iPhones, and because the HomeView will always be there and will feel familiar, I can see them actually using it. That means I could set up a full Home Assistant instance and run a detailed dashboard on a tablet in my office, then feed the scenes and devices into Apple Home so my husband and daughter can just tap to control them on a HomeView in the kitchen.
HomeView may not be the smart home computer I want Apple to make, but it is the smart home device Apple needed to make. It doesn’t have to run all the iPad apps or try to be a bigger version of my iPhone; it just needs to make the smart home accessible to everyone in the house. If Apple has pulled that off, it could be more valuable than any new smart home feature I’ve been wishing for.

articles.title: Apple's first AI features reach China in December, after a two-year wait
articles.text:
Apple plans to launch Apple Intelligence in mainland China in December with iOS 27.3, two years after the US, excluding the rebuilt Siri AI. Siri AI is also still missing in the EU, with no indication of when approval might come.
Apple will ship Apple Intelligence in mainland China in December, two years after America got it. The version Europe is still waiting for is not in it.
The launch comes with an iOS 27.3 update and excludes the rebuilt Siri AI, Bloomberg reported, citing people with knowledge of the plans.
What ships is the 2024 set. Genmoji, notification summaries, writing tools and removing objects from photos, the features widely panned at the time for not working properly.
What does not ship is this year’s work. That means the rebuilt Siri, photo expansion, upgraded Genmoji and visual intelligence in the camera, and executives are not optimistic about Siri AI arriving there soon.
Getting this far took concessions. Apple trained its own model for China with Alibaba’s help, becoming the first foreign company Beijing has approved to offer a proprietary AI model in the mainland.
The guardrails were built with Alibaba and include a filter that lets the government approve ongoing updates to the models. Baidu handles search and some Siri features.
Image generation is out. Apple’s Image Playground will not ship there, and some text generation will be limited in some apps, to comply with the rules.
Approval came slowly. The Cyberspace Administration logged the service in July, about 22 months after Apple Intelligence launched elsewhere, and permits covering recent iPhones followed on 29 September.
It nearly went out early. Apple Intelligence briefly appeared in mainland settings in March, before approval, and was pulled.
Tim Cook, now Apple’s executive chairman rather than its chief executive, attended a White House state dinner for Xi Jinping last month.
Europe is the other hard market, and the obstacle there is different. Most of this year’s features cleared on schedule in September, but Siri AI is still missing from iPhones, iPads and Apple Watches in the EU.
Nobody will say when. People with knowledge of the matter say it is unclear whether or when Apple will get approval for a local release.
The two delays are not the same. In China Apple negotiated terms and got a date, while in Europe its talks with Brussels have produced a date for nothing.

articles.title: YouTube Music launches new labels as AI-generated music floods streaming platforms | TechCrunch
articles.text:
YouTube Music announced Wednesday the rollout of a new labeling system aimed at improving transparency around songs created with the help of generative AI. Now listeners will be able to easily identify tracks created using AI, including those involved in composition and vocals.
The label will appear on the player page. Clicking on this label provides additional information about the specific role of AI in the track’s creation.
Notably, these labels will also extend to the main YouTube app.
YouTube said it collaborated with various music partners and deployed its own detection tools to identify AI-generated music. According to its help page, partners using YouTube can declare their work’s use of generative AI through one of three designations: Fully Gen AI, Partly Gen AI, or No Gen AI.
“Fully Gen AI” applies to tracks that are entirely generated by AI, while “Partly Gen AI” refers to works where artists may have incorporated AI-generated components but added their own live elements. Tracks edited using pitch-correction tools such as Auto-Tune fall under the “No Gen AI” category.
The move comes as AI-generated music rapidly expands across streaming services, and many platforms are adopting their own approaches. For instance, Apple Music has plans to introduce “Made With AI” labels as part of its AI Transparency Tags later this year. Spotify also has AI labels, as well as a music spam filter.
Deezer has taken one of the stricter stances, reporting in July that it was receiving nearly 90,000 fully AI-generated tracks daily. The platform labels detected AI-generated music and excludes it from algorithmic recommendations and editorial playlists, while also withholding royalties from fraudulent streams. The company is also working on an option to let users filter out AI-generated music.
TIDAL also labels recordings it identifies as entirely AI-generated, allows listeners to disable them, and excludes these recordings from royalty attribution.
YouTube, by contrast, is focusing on disclosure rather than blanket restrictions. Its new labels are intended to inform listeners about AI’s role in music creation, but AI involvement alone doesn’t make a track ineligible for monetization. YouTube even experiments with AI-powered music creation, including its tool Dream Track, which lets select creators generate soundtracks featuring AI-generated versions of participating artists’ voices.

articles.title: Beat the iPhone Duo pre-order rush with Apple’s Get Ready tool - Engadget
articles.text:
Beat the iPhone Duo pre-order rush with Apple’s Get Ready tool
It's basically a pre-order opportunity before the pre-order window opens.
Apple announced the iPhone Duo last month, but it won't hit stores until October 23. However, pre-orders for the highly anticipated foldable iPhone begin this week on October 16. And if you really can't wait, here's some good news: you can already get a head start on your pre-order on Apple's website. Not only that, but carriers and retailers are already advertising their special offers for the iPhone Duo — which will probably be helpful since it isn't exactly cheap. So here's how to secure your iPhone Duo with as little hassle as possible.
Securing your iPhone Duo for launch day
If you're planning to buy the iPhone Duo directly from Apple, the company has launched a tool called Get Ready, which is the best way to speed things up. Starting today (October 12), you can already choose which model you want. Go to the Apple Online Store or use the Apple Store app and look for the iPhone Duo. Choose a color (Star White or Night Sky) and storage capacity (from 256GB to 2TB). Then, choose your carrier, decide whether or not you want to trade in your old phone and maybe add a few accessories to your purchase as well — you'll probably want to protect your new $2,000 phone with a case. AppleCare+ is also a good deal, and you can sign up for it from the purchase screen.
When all that's set, Get Ready saves you some pre-order anxiety by letting you set up a payment method and your shipping address now, before the purchase window opens on Friday. As soon as it does, Apple will place your order and ensure that you receive your new iPhone in time for launch day. Waiting until Friday to pre-order your iPhone could end up delaying shipping if you aren't quick enough, since there's usually strong demand for new products. Also, rumors suggest that there won't be many iPhone Duo units available at launch. If you use Apple's Get Ready, your chances of receiving the iPhone Duo on October 23 increase considerably.
Where to buy the iPhone Duo
Once again, you can buy your iPhone Duo directly from Apple — it's usually the easiest option, especially if you don't want to buy it tied to a specific plan or carrier. Apple is offering up to $885 in credit when you trade in an eligible iPhone, so giving up your old iPhone might be a good way to make the Duo a little less expensive. The full price starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model and can go as high as $3,199 for the 2TB model.
You can also split payments over up to 24 months, so buying the 256GB model would cost you $83.29 per month. If you sign up for the new Apple Upgrade program, the cost drops to $57.99 per month. Just now that after two years, you'll have to hand your iPhone back to Apple, pay the remaining balance to keep it or upgrade to a new device and keep paying.
Carriers are also already announcing their deals for the iPhone Duo. AT&T, for example, offers up to $1,200 in eligible trade-ins, and if you order online, you'll also earn an extra $200 per line on your plan. Best Buy will also have special deals for the iPhone Duo launch, with prices starting at $55.96 per month on an installment plan with AT&T. It's worth comparing each of these offers side by side to see which one works best for you.

articles.title: Eight states sue OpenAI, saying ChatGPT isn’t safe for kids
articles.text:
OpenAI is facing a new wave of lawsuits from eight US states that accuse the company of harming children and misleading customers about the safety of ChatGPT, as reported earlier by Reuters. The lawsuits, filed separately by Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho, and Montana, allege OpenAI unlawfully put profits over safety when developing ChatGPT.
Eight states sue OpenAI, saying ChatGPT isn’t safe for kids
OpenAI is accused of misleading the public about its chatbot’s safety and putting everyone at risk.
The string of complaints claims that OpenAI violated local consumer protection laws by failing to warn customers about the dangers of ChatGPT, citing several lawsuits filed by the family members of teens and adults that allege the AI chatbot played a role in their loved ones’ deaths. They allege that while OpenAI misleadingly presented ChatGPT as a “safe, youth-appropriate tool that puts safety first,” it was actually “dangerous to vulnerable users” — including by “degrading critical thinking skills, encouraging paranoias and delusions, offering dangerous medical advice, and promoting unhealthy behaviors and relationships.”
Additionally, the states accuse OpenAI of collecting data from minors and not doing enough to keep underage users from using the chatbot. The lawsuits also cite recent rogue AI hacking incidents as evidence of OpenAI’s alleged “recklessness.”
“OpenAI has devolved from its original mission as a public-first nonprofit that prioritized safety into a cautionary tale about what can happen when the development of a tool as powerful as AI is driven not by safety, but by a profit‑at‑all‑costs mindset that sidelines essential safeguards,” Arizona’s lawsuit claims.
In an emailed statement to The Verge, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri says the company has “built industry-leading age-specific protections” into ChatGPT:
While no system can be perfect, we’ll continue to work with experts to inform our work and build additional safeguards, such as the parental controls, break reminders and age-appropriate model protections that exist today. We’re committed to working with states on advancing pragmatic AI policies that apply to the entire AI industry - not just one company.
The states are asking the courts to force OpenAI to pay a series of civil penalties and to stop misleading the public about the safety of ChatGPT. Some states are also seeking the deletion of unlawfully collected personal data.
Update, October 14th: Added a statement from OpenAI.

articles.title: The charged OpenAI engineer had a one-way ticket out of the US, a filing shows
articles.text:
Abdulrahman Alfozan, the OpenAI engineer charged over a hidden recording device, had one-way tickets to Saudi Arabia booked for three days after his arrest, according to a court filing. He has entered no reported plea and is presumed innocent.
The OpenAI engineer charged over a hidden recording device had a one-way ticket out of the United States booked for three days after his arrest. A court filing shows it.
Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, had tickets to Saudi Arabia via Istanbul, with his wife and another family member, Bloomberg reported. He was arrested on 9 October and the flight was booked for 12 October.
The filing was the government’s argument for sealing the case. Prosecutors wrote on 8 October that he had the means, and would have an incentive, to flee if he learned of it before his arrest.
He is charged with using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications, which carries up to five years. He has entered no reported plea and is presumed innocent.
The device itself was reported last week. It was found on 30 September behind a television in an executive conference room, and a second was allegedly found on 5 October in a bag left unattended.
OpenAI says no model weights, source code or customer data were taken. It says it used its own models to understand the device and identify who planted it.
Its finance chief was asked about the case in Dublin on Wednesday. She thanked the security team and declined to give details.
What is new is who is prosecuting it. The FBI is investigating, the National Security Division’s counterintelligence section assisted, and the US attorney called it a matter of national security.
The case is tied to a presidential memorandum on American leadership in superintelligence. Europe has no equivalent instrument, though OpenAI is adding 200 Dublin jobs and holds offices in Paris, Brussels and London.
No foreign government is alleged to have directed him. No motive is alleged in the material released, and nothing says what the device captured.
The encryption may be part of that. Its contents were encrypted when OpenAI found it, and nothing released says whether they have since been read.
The complaint says he had no authority to enter the room, which hosted meetings on confidential technical, commercial and strategic matters. He joined in July 2025 and was dismissed the day he was arrested.
He is next due before Magistrate Judge Alex Tse in San Francisco on 19 October.
